detail.abstract:
Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) in biomedicine must be explainable to ensure trust, accountability, and safety. However, most explainable AI (XAI) approaches are evaluated primarily on technical grounds, with limited systematic assessment and reliable metrics, hindering translation into practice.

Objective: This study aims to identify and categorize XAI systems for biomedical data that fulfill criteria for evaluation readiness, defined by output demonstration, input data availability, and practical applicability.

Methods: A systematic mapping study was conducted using a Scopus search from 2020 to 2025, retrieving 1,178 journal and conference papers. Restricting to 2023 to 2025 yielded 780. Screening identified 27 systems meeting evaluation readiness criteria, classified by AI evaluation, AI method, agnosticism, data type, input samples, medical field, medical use case, scope, stage, XAI evaluation, XAI method, and XAI technique.

Results: Imaging-oriented XAI systems dominate, with 63% (n = 17) using radiology or histopathology pipelines and visual heatmaps such as Grad-CAM and saliency maps. Tabular (n = 4) and graph-based (n = 3) approaches are less common. Feature relevance methods, especially SHAP (n = 6), prevail. Grad-CAM is frequent in imaging (n = 4), while graph-based techniques are emerging (n = 4). Evaluation strategies emphasize functionality-grounded approaches, 52% (n = 14), with fewer application-grounded (n = 11) and rare human-grounded (n = 2) assessments. Most XAI systems provide code and, in some cases, web applications, enabling reproducibility, e.g., MICA and CIS2MS.

Conclusion: Evaluation-ready XAI systems in biomedicine are scarce, imaging-dominated, and specialized. Local explanations and architecture modification methods are underused, and cross-domain benchmarking is essential. The lack of standardized XAI metrics limits comparability. This mapping offers a starting point for validation. Its Scopus-only search, single-round coding, and assumed evaluation readiness criteria motivate broader search, multistage review, and human-grounded research.

title: Risk Sharing through Buybacks
affiliations: Korea University Business School and The Chinese University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Risk Sharing through Buybacks
detail.abstract: We provide economy-wide evidence that buyback agreements are pervasive in production networks and reallocate risk and output when demand collapses. Using Korean value-added tax invoices from 2017Q1-2021Q4, we identify buyback relationships as supplier-customer dyads with pre-COVID reciprocal flows. Buyback dyads are geographically proximate, trade more frequently and at larger volumes, and sustain longer ties than one-way dyads. Although only 4.2% of active dyads exhibit such flows, they mediate 46.9% of B2B sales and link nearly half of firms. A difference-indifferences design around COVID-19, estimated on entropy-balanced samples with dyad and firm-year fixed effects, shows that along buyback links, reciprocal sales rise by 10.4% and forward sales fall by 3.7% relative to non-buyback dyads, consistent with customers exercising the return option. Suppliers subsequently redeploy inventory, initially to existing partners and then via new outlets, offsetting losses. Formation follows a capacity-need logic: riskier buyers match with more stable suppliers, and only suppliers with high-risk-absorbing capacity honor commitments under stress. Overall, buybacks operate as decentralized insurance, buffering downstream firms in bad states while enabling upstream reallocation that sustains trade.

title: Global Maritime Supply Determinants, Dynamics, and Macroeconomic Impacts
affiliations: University of International Business and Economics, University of International Business and Economics, University of International Business and Economics, Tsinghua University and Tsinghua University

detail.title: Global Maritime Supply Determinants, Dynamics, and Macroeconomic Impacts
detail.abstract: We construct a Maritime Supply Index (MSI) using high-frequency Automatic Identification System (AIS) data from container ships to monitor weekly changes in the global provision of shipping services. The MSI captures multiple dimensions of maritime activity, including shipping capacity, vessel speed adjustments, non-blank sailings, rerouting, and congestion at ports and key chokepoints such as the Suez and Panama Canals. Spanning 2017–2024, the index provides a real-time indicator of global maritime supply and reflects the effects of major disruptions —including the China–U.S. trade war, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia–Ukraine war, and the Red Sea crisis— on containerized trade. Our decomposition shows that vessel speed adjustments are the primary driver of short-term fluctuations, supplemented by port congestion and geopolitical rerouting. Integrating the MSI with shipping prices and macroeconomic indicators, we disentangle shipping demand and supply shocks and trace their inflationary consequences. We find that the 2021 price surge was mainly demand-driven, the 2022 collapse reflected both falling demand and recovering supply, and U.S. inflation responded to supply shocks with a delay, reflecting nominal rigidity.

title: Forecast Dispersion and the Price Impact of Macroeconomic News
affiliations: Tilburg University - Department of Finance

detail.title: Forecast Dispersion and the Price Impact of Macroeconomic News
detail.abstract: While a large literature in macro-finance examines how financial markets respond to macroeconomic news, little is known about how the composition of the forecaster pool shapes these responses. Using data on 25 major U.S. macroeconomic announcements, I document that forecast dispersion has a strong negative effect on market reactions, challenging the conventional interpretation of dispersion as a proxy for uncertainty. To reconcile this puzzle, I develop a noisy rational expectations model in which the informational content of dispersion depends on the share of experienced analysts. When the forecaster pool is primarily experienced, low dispersion indicates precise pre-announcement information, reducing the announcement's price impact. Conversely, when the pool is inexperienced, low dispersion reflects shrinkage toward noisy common information, increasing price impact. Using lagged analyst experience as an instrument, I confirm that the relationship between dispersion and price impact switches sign depending on the share of experienced analysts. These findings reveal an important channel through which analyst heterogeneity affects price discovery.

title: Nature-Related Risk Perception of Smallholder Farmers and Implications for Global Agricultural Supply Chain Sustainability
affiliations: Deakin University, Deakin University - Centre for Integrative Ecology, Deakin University, Deakin University and Deakin University

detail.title: Nature-Related Risk Perception of Smallholder Farmers and Implications for Global Agricultural Supply Chain Sustainability
detail.abstract: Smallholder farmers are vital to global agricultural supply chains but remain highly vulnerable to nature-related risks due to direct exposure and limited benefits from value chains. This study examines how smallholder tea farmers in northern Vietnam perceive nature-related risks, including observed and experienced changes in ecosystem services, their future perceptions of nature-related risks, and the factors influencing these views, using social surveys grounded in nature-related risk concepts and Protection Motivation Theory. Farmers observed declines in soil health and water availability, as well as climate change and pest pressures, which are affecting tea yield and quality. While soil and water issues were seen as less immediate, they remain important longer-term risks. Risk experiences, farming practices, adaptation actions, socioeconomic characteristics, and information shaped perceptions. Heavy fertiliser use raised concerns about soil degradation, while implementing irrigation systems reduced perceived vulnerability to extreme weather. Information from training courses influenced farmers’ risk awareness. These subjective nature-related risk perceptions may differ from the objective risks mapped by spatial models, but they strongly influence farmers’ adaptation intentions. Nature-related risks can ripple through entire agrifood value chains from the farm to the customer. Engaging smallholders directly in nature-related risk assessments could better capture local risks and inform sustainable value chain management for value chains that depend on smallholders, such as tea, cocoa, and coffee.

title: A Simple Model of Geopolitical Risk and Sanctions
affiliations: Research Centre and Deutsche Bundesbank

detail.title: A Simple Model of Geopolitical Risk and Sanctions
detail.abstract: Geopolitical risk (GPR) shocks that trigger the imposition of sanctions tend to lower output and raise inflation in the sanctioned country. We develop a three-equation small open economy New Keynesian model where GPR shocks are modeled as negative productivity shocks and sanctions manifest as import tariffs in response to GPR increases. We calibrate the GPR process, sanction rule, and interest rate rule to match the observed dynamics of the GPR index, output, inflation, and the policy rate in Russian data. The sanction response to GPR allows the resulting model to capture the empirical impulse responses well. Additionally, we find that Russia’s monetary policy rule is more accommodative than prescribed by the standard Taylor rule. While this may reflect policy preferences, recent theoretical results indicate that such a policy stance may be optimal when sanctions act as cost-push shocks that shift the Phillips Curve.

title: "Holistic Impacts of AICS Assistance: Addressing Clients' Needs beyond Financial Relief"

detail.title: "Holistic Impacts of AICS Assistance: Addressing Clients' Needs beyond Financial Relief"
detail.abstract: This study investigates the holistic impacts of the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) program in Zamboanga City, examining how social welfare interventions address client needs beyond immediate financial relief. Grounded in Psychosocial Theory, which emphasizes the interaction between individual psychological functioning and the social environment, the study explores how comprehensive support fosters resilience, adaptive coping, and household stability among beneficiaries. A mixed-methods design was employed, with quantitative data collected on financial aid distribution, utilization, and beneficiary satisfaction, and qualitative insights obtained through in-depth interviews with both beneficiaries and social workers. Findings indicate that while monetary assistance provides essential short-term relief, the program's broader effects-including psychosocial support, referrals to health services, engagement with livelihood and skills programs, and follow-up counseling-significantly enhance overall well-being. Beneficiaries reported reduced stress, improved coping strategies, strengthened family cohesion, and increased participation in community activities, highlighting the multidimensional nature of program impacts. The study underscores the importance of integrating economic, social, and psychosocial interventions in social welfare program design to achieve sustainable outcomes. In practice, social workers play a pivotal role in facilitating access to community resources, providing counseling, and ensuring follow-up support, thereby enhancing resilience at both individual and household levels. These findings propose that the AICS program can be optimized through a holistic, psychosocial approach, ensuring that vulnerable populations receive comprehensive, long-term support that addresses both immediate crises and ongoing adaptive needs.

detail.abstract:
This study examines the impact of decentralized finance (DeFi) on the banking industry in Nigeria. DeFi, which leverages blockchain technology to offer financial services without traditional intermediaries, has the potential to improve traditional banking systems. The research focuses on understanding the challenges and opportunities DeFi presents for the Nigerian banking sector, including its ability to promote financial inclusion, reduce transaction costs, and enhance the operation of banks and existing business models within the country.

Interviews were conducted with Nigerian professionals from both the DeFi and traditional banking sectors, including those in marketing, data analysis, and technology development. The results highlight that while DeFi offers significant potential benefits, its adoption in the Nigerian banking system remains limited due to regulatory uncertainty, insufficient technological infrastructure, and security concerns. The study finds that collaboration between traditional banks and DeFi platforms, alongside clear regulatory frameworks, could facilitate the integration of decentralized financial services in Nigeria. The research concludes by offering insights into how Nigerian banks might adapt to the rise of DeFi, contributing to ongoing discussions on the future of finance in emerging markets.

title: Can Regulatory Sandbox Boost Bank Profitability?

detail.title: Can Regulatory Sandbox Boost Bank Profitability?
detail.abstract: This paper exploits the FinTech Innovation Regulatory Pilot Program (the regulatory sandbox) launched by the People’s Bank of China at the end of 2019 as a quasi-natural experiment. Using panel data from 31 pilot banks over the period 2011–2022, we investigate the impact of this policy on commercial banks’ profitability and the underlying mechanisms. The results show that the regulatory sandbox policy significantly enhances the profitability of commercial banks, and the findings remain robust across multiple robustness checks. Further mechanism analysis indicates that the policy improves bank profitability by fostering the adoption of foundational FinTech technologies and promoting innovation in FinTech business practices. The heterogeneity analysis reveals that the effect is more pronounced among banks with smaller asset scales. Moreover, the policy’s impact differs across ownership types of commercial banks, highlighting the complexity and multi-dimensional nature of its effectiveness.

title: Repo Collateral Reuse and Liquidity Windfalls

detail.title: Repo Collateral Reuse and Liquidity Windfalls
detail.abstract: Collateral reuse in repo markets helps entities meet short-term funding needs, maintain market efficiency, and anchor collateral valuations, although it creates risks through interconnectedness. A prominent view in the literature is that securities dealers use their market position to obtain temporary free-cash wedges from differences in collateral requirements when reusing collateral, so-called “liquidity windfalls”. By affecting dealers’ funding structures, such windfalls could influence yield curve determination, leverage, and monetary policy transmission. Yet the evidence has been largely theoretical, with limited empirical work. Using a novel, confidential regulatory dataset on European Securities Financing Transactions, this study helps fill that gap. We find that about 11.6% of European repo transaction volume relies on reused securities, averaging more than 49 billion euros per day. Moreover, contrary to the liquidity windfalls hypothesis, dealers do not seem to systematically obtain extra liquidity through collateral reuse in repos.

title: Joining Forces: Why Banks Syndicate Credit
affiliations: University of Zurich, University of Zurich - Department Finance and European Central Bank (ECB)

detail.title: Joining Forces: Why Banks Syndicate Credit
detail.abstract: Banks can grant loans to firms bilaterally or in syndicates. We study this choice by combining bilateral loan data with syndicated loan data. We show that loan size alone does not adequately explain syndication. Instead, banks’ ability to manage risks and firm riskiness drive the choice to syndicate. Banks are more likely to syndicate loans if their risk-bearing capacity is low and if screening and monitoring come at a high cost. Syndicated loans are more expensive and more sensitive to loan risk than bilateral loans. Our findings contradict the hypothesis that reputable borrowers graduate to the syndicated loan market.

detail.abstract: We propose a novel mathematical framework for understanding and potentially predicting financial crises by representing monetary systems as complex numbers. By defining Z = R + i•C, where R represents the real economy and C represents credit/cryptocurrency systems, we introduce a geometric interpretation where the angle θ = arctan(C/R) serves as a crisis indicator. Preliminary observations suggest that historical crises (2000, 2008, 2022) occurred when θ exceeded approximately 80°. This framework offers a unified, quantifiable approach to systemic risk assessment and introduces the concept of "null intersection" (Fiat ∩ Crypto = Ø) as a theoretical foundation for understanding monetary system incompatibility.

detail.abstract: The structural crisis of legitimacy within the United States constitutional order no longer arises merely from political division or administrative dysfunction. It stems from an institutional silence—the gradual disappearance of citizens from the procedures through which legality itself is produced. While the Constitution begins with the phrase “We the People,” modern governance has confined the people to spectatorship. Immigration policy, perhaps more than any other field, exposes this paradox: decisions determining who belongs to the nation are made without the participation of the nation’s members. This study reconstructs that missing link between sovereignty and participation through a constitutional analysis of the Hundred Overseers Pathway, a citizen-supervised framework for democratic legalization proposed in 2025. The paper argues that such a system is not only compatible with, but deeply rooted in, the U.S. Constitution. It traces the intellectual lineage of citizen judgment from the jury clause of the Sixth Amendment to contemporary doctrines of due process, equal protection, and popular sovereignty. Through this inquiry, the paper establishes that constitutional legitimacy can emerge not only from representative deliberation but from structured participation—a civic mechanism in which citizens exercise oversight under legislated authority. Rather than redefining sovereignty, the model restores it: it transforms legality from an administrative function into a democratic process observable, verifiable, and reviewable by the governed themselves. The constitutional foundations of this model reveal that the survival of the republic depends less on the perfection of institutions than on their ability to include the people in the ongoing authorship of law.

title: A Machine Learning Approach to Real Time Identification of Turning Points in Monetary Aggregates M1 and M3
affiliations: European Central Bank (ECB) and European Central Bank (ECB)

detail.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Real Time Identification of Turning Points in Monetary Aggregates M1 and M3
detail.abstract: Monetary aggregates provide valuable information about the monetary policy transmission and the business cycle. This paper applies machine learning methods, namely Learning Vector Quantisation (LVQ) and its distinction-sensitive extension (DSLVQ), to identify turning points in euro area M1 and M3. We benchmark performance against the Bry–Boschan algorithm and standard classifiers. Our results show that LVQ detects M1 turning points with only a three-month delay, halving the six-month confirmation lag of Bry–Boschan dating. DSLVQ delivers comparable accuracy while offering interpretability: it assigns weights to the sources of broad money growth, showing that lending to households and firms, as well as Eurosystem asset purchases when present, are the main drivers of turning points in M3. The findings are robust across parameter choices, bootstrap designs, alternative performance metrics, and comparator models. These results demonstrate that machine learning can yield more timely and interpretable signals from monetary aggregates. For policymakers, this approach enhances the information set available for assessing near-term economic dynamics and understanding the transmission of monetary policy.

detail.abstract: We develop a theory of demand economics for an era of material abundance. The binding constraint on growth has shifted from insufficient aggregate demand to inadequate demand-tier upgrading. Our result is that, the new engine of growth lies in upgrading the demand hierarchy: higher-tier demands generate larger value-creation multipliers. The key mechanism is education-driven utility management. Education transforms the social utility function, raises the utility of higher-tier goods, and directs resources toward higher-value domains; this warrants a policy reorientation away from short-run aggregate stimulus toward education-centered, long-horizon investments in human capital. Methodologically, we build an estimable general-equilibrium framework.

detail.abstract: The traditional wisdom that price momentum which ranks stocks’ raw trailing returns is crash-prone fails to differentiate the various drivers of stocks’ past performances. As such, we compare the persistence of different sources of stocks’ price momentum discerned from applying factor-based performance attribution to their trailing 12-month returns. Our empirical analysis shows that beta- and country-driven price trends were not robust while style and industry momentum persisted both over the intermediate and, more strongly, short-term. Stock-specific momentum persisted over the intermediate term but strongly reverted over the short term; it was subsumed as a stand-alone strategy by both industry and style momentum and should be downweighed when optimizing a momentum signal for persistence. Our results suggest that style momentum is mostly a proxy for static factor tilts while industry and stock-specific momentum appear a separate anomaly that is strongest conditional on low-volatility market regimes. Their premium may reflect investor underreaction to economic shifts to which stocks’ exposures are imperfectly captured by binary industry classifications. Our results corroborate a strand of the extant literature through the novel lens of exactly decomposing the cross-section of stocks’ price momentum; contradicting findings are explained by methodological differences.

title: IDRIC Frontiers Report: Industrial Heat and Energy Efficiency

title: Supply Chain Finance and Firm Employment: Evidence from China​

detail.title: Supply Chain Finance and Firm Employment: Evidence from China​
detail.abstract: We examine whether supply chain finance (SCF) stabilizes corporate employment in the context of China’s policy agenda emphasizing financial stability and stable employment. Using an annual panel of China’s A-share listed firms from 2008–2024, we estimate the effect of SCF on employment and evaluate the underlying mechanisms. We find that SCF increases firm employment. Mechanism tests indicate that SCF operates through three mechanisms—enhancing technological innovation, relaxing financing constraints, and improving supply chain management efficiency. The effect is stronger among faster-growing firms, firms with greater financialization, and those with weaker core operating performance. Further analyses show that SCF shifts labor demand toward highly skilled and highly educated workers and increases average employee compensation. Overall, the study clarifies the mechanisms linking SCF to corporate employment, adds to the evidence on SCF’s economic consequences, and offers empirical support for policies that leverage SCF to stabilize employment.

title: How Does Digital Transformation Affect the Risk-Taking of Commercial Banks? Empirical Evidence from China
affiliations: Zhongnan University of Economics and Law and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: How Does Digital Transformation Affect the Risk-Taking of Commercial Banks? Empirical Evidence from China
detail.abstract: In the current context of increasing economic, trade, and geopolitical uncertainties, coupled with a sharp rise in global financial risks, the Chinese banking sector plays a crucial role in maintaining both domestic and international financial stability. This paper focuses on the empowerment of financial technology and utilizes data from 186 commercial banks in China spanning from 2010 to 2023 to systematically explore the impact of digital transformation on banks’ risk-taking behavior and its underlying mechanisms. Empirical results indicate that digital transformation significantly suppresses risk-taking among commercial banks. In terms of mechanism analysis, this study innovatively verifies that digital transformation inhibits risk exposure through two interrelated pathways: reducing operational management costs and enhancing business diversification levels. Further analysis reveals that increased government regulatory pressure and improved internal governance effectiveness can strengthen the risk suppression effect of digital transformation; notably, this suppressive effect is more pronounced in small banks or local commercial banks. This research provides important theoretical foundations and decision-making references for both practical implementations of digital transformation within commercial banks and policy formulation aimed at mitigating financial risks.

title: Endogenous Regulation of Selection Pressure: A Minimal Game-Theoretical Model
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Endogenous Regulation of Selection Pressure: A Minimal Game-Theoretical Model
detail.abstract: Selection pressure, determining which individuals survive and reproduce, is traditionally regarded as an exogenous property of the environment. However, growing evidence from the Extended Evolutionary Synthesis (EES) suggests that the strength of selection can, to some extent, be modulated by the organisms themselves. In this paper, we propose a minimal game-theoretical model that formalizes the concept of \textit{endogenous selection pressure}. In the model, individuals collectively determine the intensity of selection through their actions: each agent “votes” to either intensify or relax selection depending on its relative fitness rank. The aggregate outcome of these decisions defines the number of reproducers, $k$, which is inversely related to the overall strength of selection. We analytically derive all pure strategy Nash equilibria (PSNE) of the game and examine their properties. By internalizing selection as a population-level emergent variable, the framework provides a tractable formalization of key principles from the EES and offers a foundation for exploring evolutionary dynamics that arise under the presence of endogenous selection pressure.

title: Process Optimization and Structural Analysis of Humic Acid Extracted from Low-Rank Coal in Xinjiang, China
affiliations: Henan Polytechnic University, Henan Polytechnic University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Henan Polytechnic University and Henan Polytechnic University

detail.title: Process Optimization and Structural Analysis of Humic Acid Extracted from Low-Rank Coal in Xinjiang, China
detail.abstract: In order to enhance the extraction efficiency of humic acid (HA) from low-rank coal, an orthogonal experimental design was employed to optimize the parameters of the alkali hydrothermal extraction process. Key parameters, including extraction temperature, extraction time, alkali concentration, and solid-to-liquid ratio, were systematically varied to determine the optimal conditions. The influence of these factors on HA yield was evaluated through intuitive analysis and range analysis. Under the optimized conditions, the HA yields obtained from four lignite samples collected from different regions of Xinjiang—Akesu (AKS), Naomaohu (NMH), Dananhu (DNH), and Santanghu (STH)—were 76.31%, 64.98%, 41.33%, and 63.53%, respectively. Furthermore, the physicochemical properties and structural characteristics of the extracted HAs were analyzed using elemental analysis, acidic functional group determination, UV–Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, XRD, and XPS. The results indicated that the STH-derived HA (STH-HA) exhibited the highest aromaticity and the most pronounced degree of condensation. The aromatic condensation of the four HAs followed the order: STH-HA > DNH-HA > AKS-HA > NMH-HA. Overall, this study not only provides optimized conditions for the efficient extraction of humic acid from low-rank coal but also offers theoretical guidance for its further utilization.

title: Temperature-controlled extraction of humic acid from Shendong subbituminous coal and its structure-activity relationship: Pyrolysis characteristics, agricultural applications, and residue pyrolysis recycling
affiliations: Xijing University - School of Science, Northwest University - School of Chemical Engineering, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Northwest University - School of Chemical Engineering

detail.title: Temperature-controlled extraction of humic acid from Shendong subbituminous coal and its structure-activity relationship: Pyrolysis characteristics, agricultural applications, and residue pyrolysis recycling
detail.abstract: Humic acids (HAs) are currently highly effective amendments for ecological cultivation and the improvement of infertile soils. This study investigated the effects of different extraction temperatures (50-200 °C) on the extraction rates and structures of fulvic acid (FA), brown humic acid (ZA), and black humic acid (BA) from subbituminous coal. Results indicate that high temperatures significantly enhance HAs extraction rates. At 200 °C, the extraction rate of HAs reached three times that at 50 °C (with FA increasing 4.6 times), while the total acidic group content of FA rose from 8.63 mmol/g to 10.37 mmol/g. Characterization via FTIR, UV-Vis, fluorescence spectroscopy, TG, and Py-GC/MS revealed that FA contains abundant carboxyl and phenolic hydroxyl compounds. With increasing temperature, its molecular structure undergoes a gradual transformation from aliphatic side chains and O-containing functional groups to a condensed state dominated by aromatic nuclei. Based on this, a “triple-layer core-shell” molecular structural model for HAs was proposed. Wheat cultivation experiments confirmed that FA extracted at high temperatures significantly promoted wheat growth and drought resistance, with the most developed root systems observed under FA extracted at 200 °C. Furthermore, although the content of oxygenated compounds decreased after pyrolysis of the residue, it still released large amounts of high-value-added products such as aromatics and alkanes. The residue exhibited the highest thermal stability at an extraction temperature of 150 °C, demonstrating considerable application potential. This study elucidates the effects of extraction temperature on HAs yield and structure, providing new theoretical foundations for coal utilization in ecological agriculture.

title: When storms strike: The moderating role of Tobin’s Q in investment resilience
affiliations: City University of New York (CUNY) - Economics Department, University of Economics Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, University of Economics Ho Chi Minh City and University of Economics Ho Chi Minh City

detail.title: When storms strike: The moderating role of Tobin’s Q in investment resilience
detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between storms and corporate investment, highlighting the moderating role of Tobin’s Q when storms occur. Using a panel dataset of 10,838 firm-year observations from 1,476 Vietnamese listed firms during the 2013–2023 period, the study explores how firms’ market-to-book ratio (Tobin’s Q) influences their resilience to environmental shocks. Consistent with the theory, a higher Tobin’s Q—indicating stronger growth opportunities, market optimism, and lower replacement costs—mitigates the negative impact of storms on physical capital investment. We see a similar pattern in short term investment – decreases after storms, but firms with higher Tobin’s Q see smaller decreases.  As one might expect, replacement investments increase post-storm. To shed light on this effect, we decompose Tobin’s Q into its numerator (market value) and denominator (book value or “replacement costs”) and find that new physical investments decline with pre-storm replacement costs and increase with pre-storm market value. This effect is captured by the ratio of the two measures of value—we divide the effect along the point Q=1, where Q>1 indicates relatively low replacement costs and high market optimism. These Q>1 firms show significantly more post-storm capital investment, while those with Q<1 see significantly less. These findings emphasize the capital-driven nature of firm responses and highlight the role of investment efficiency and growth opportunities. Robustness tests with various storm measures confirm the findings, and the effects are concentrated in storm-affected regions, though storms may also divert investment away from non-storm regions during extreme weather periods.

title: Medical Expenditure Risk and Household Portfolios: Evidence from an Insurance Reform in China
affiliations: Central University of Finance and Economics, University of Edinburgh - Business School and Bank of Qingdao

detail.title: Medical Expenditure Risk and Household Portfolios: Evidence from an Insurance Reform in China
detail.abstract: We examine how reductions in medical expenditure risk shape household portfolio choices. Exploiting the 2017 inclusion of cancer treatment drugs in China's National Basic Medical Insurance Medicine List, we implement a difference-indifferences design comparing high-risk and low-risk insured individuals. The results show that households facing elevated cancer risk became significantly more likely to hold risky assets after the reform. These findings provide novel causal evidence that mitigating health-related background risk encourages financial risk-taking.

title: Greenhouse Gas Emission, Corporate Capital Structure, and Financial Decisions: US State-Level Evidence

detail.title: Greenhouse Gas Emission, Corporate Capital Structure, and Financial Decisions: US State-Level Evidence
detail.abstract: For the first time, this study quantifies the long-term effects of greenhouse gas [GHG] emissions on corporate capital structures. Using US state-level data, I find that GHG exposure has adverse consequences for the capital structure, with a persistently predicted decrease in corporate financial leverage. The treatment effects of GHG exposure are exceptionally robust, even when we control for a battery of endogenous and exogenous drivers. Firms that are treated experience chronic economic downgrades and liquidity shortfalls. Shrinking cash reserves induce firms to decrease corporate payouts for both dividends and share repurchases. Trade credit serves as an alternative source of liquidity; however, it poses challenges for firms with higher biodiversity risks that are prone to natural disasters, particularly since the implementation of the Paris Agreement. With increasing financial distress, such long-term GHG exposure consequently renders firms financially constrained, forcing them to rely on external finances with a constant decrease in corporate leverage. As climate change brings both opportunities and risks to firms, our study provides ground-breaking evidence for major corporate finance literature streams. With multiple novelties, our hypotheses tested are empirically robust, which is fundamentally critical to future studies.

title: Assessing the Alignment of Carbon Metrics with AI Systems: Pathways Toward Green Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: Regional Advisory Commision on Financial Markets

detail.title: Assessing the Alignment of Carbon Metrics with AI Systems: Pathways Toward Green Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming various fields—from healthcare and climate science to logistics and finance—while also boosting productivity growth. As AI's economic and societal importance grows, so does awareness of the environmental issues it presents. For example, the carbon footprint of AI training workloads is significant enough to affect global warming. Additionally, emissions from AI-enabled components (such as recommendation systems) can surpass those from direct AI training. These concerns have led to research into Green AI, which focuses on improving algorithmic efficiency without sacrificing performance (Wu et al., 2021).

Carbon-metric reporting plays a pivotal role in advancing Green AI, yet remains poorly aligned with existing AI systems. Definitions of carbon metrics applicable to AI and widely used in lifecycle assessment (LCA) studies (Debnath et al., 2023) must be provided. Candidate metrics include energy intensity, emissions per inference, lifecycle emissions from the envelope and hardware, and embodied carbon in hardware. Specifying operational boundaries (data centres, edge devices; training versus inference) and temporal scope (lifetime stages; time horizon) is likewise crucial for enabling multiple research avenues, monitoring the full spectrum of emissions associated with AI throughout the materials economy, and helping stakeholders understand the prevailing carbon-influence mechanisms (Debnath et al., 2023).

The immense and growing energy demands of AI systems, both during training and inference, make their carbon footprints consequential to climate and sustainability objectives. Prioritising emissions reduction in AI routine selection, design, and deployment is vital for establishing system-level carbon targets by decoupling performance from lifetime emissions across the cloud and materials economies. The urgency of pursuing such decoupling can be further assessed through accompanying lifecycle LCA mapping of cradle-to-grave material flows and CO2e (g), which are pivotal in emissions formation. Examining how Fourier-based methods, which can be schematised as operator-structured, could contribute to such decoupling is similarly warranted.

Carbon metrics that report on the computational and operational demands of AI systems (e.g., energy and G-CO₂-equivalent) play a crucial role in these efforts. Recent findings indicate that various algorithmic classes can yield substantial relative reductions—exceeding 50%—in the number of units involved without sacrificing performance, suggesting that lower-level architectures could achieve comparable gains. The deepening synergy between AI and climate science has further motivated a holistic investigation of the information-theoretic limits on enhancing AI systems while minimising associated digital footprints at both the hardware and algorithmic levels.

title: Debt Covenant Violations and Corporate Financing and Investment Decisions: A Financial Statement Decomposition Approach
affiliations: Hanken School of Economics and Aalto University

detail.title: Debt Covenant Violations and Corporate Financing and Investment Decisions: A Financial Statement Decomposition Approach
detail.abstract: This study examines how debt covenant violations affect corporate financing and investment behavior. We shed new light on this question by applying a regression-based financial-statement decomposition that jointly maps financing and investment flows across firms. We find that violations are followed by significant increases in cash holdings and net repayments to debt holders, accompanied by modest reductions in equity distributions. The net effect is an increase in free cash flow, offering novel evidence on how covenant violations reshape internal liquidity. On the investment side, capital expenditures decline immediately, while research and development and lease expenses remain stable. Acquisition activity shows no short-term change but declines over the two- and three-year horizons, consistent with a gradual retreat from discretionary external growth. Overall, our findings demonstrate that creditor intervention selectively constrains financial policies while preserving strategic and operational investments.

title: Bootstrapping Option Risk Premiums
affiliations: City University of New York, Baruch College - Zicklin School of Business - Department of Economics and Finance

detail.title: Bootstrapping Option Risk Premiums
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a bootstrapping procedure for estimating conditional option risk premiums and conditional option return variance and covariance. The procedure scales the daily security return with the option implied volatility to filter out the stochastic volatility effect and extract the return innovation. It estimates a nonlinear mean-reverting dynamics to extract the volatility innovation on each floating implied volatility series. Jointly bootstrapping the return and implied volatility innovations captures their co-movements and constructs the security price and implied volatility paths for option excess return calculation over any investment horizon. Applying the procedure to the history of over-the-counter currency options shows that the bootstrapped option return risk and risk premium vary strongly both across contracts and over time. The bootstrapped option risk premium predicts the future realized option excess return in accordance with the expectation hypothesis. Mean-variance investment in the option contracts based on the bootstrapped option risk premium and covariance generates high risk-adjusted returns.

title: The Accountability Amplification Hypothesis Fails: Digital Tools Do Not Improve Governance Across Institutional Contexts
affiliations: Panjab University

detail.title: The Accountability Amplification Hypothesis Fails: Digital Tools Do Not Improve Governance Across Institutional Contexts

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author(s) declare no potential conflicts of interest with respect to the research, authorship, and/or publication of this article.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based on publicly available secondary data and did not require ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: The theory that digital tools amplify citizen accountability to improve governance is a cornerstone of modern public administration. Yet large-scale empirical evidence for this relationship remains scarce and often ignores contextual differences. An analysis of a 15country, 25-year panel dataset tests a moderated mediation hypothesis across High-Income, BRICS, and Low-Income nations. The findings are stark. The hypothesized mediation effect of Digital Enablement on the relationship between Institutional Accountability and Government Effectiveness is not statistically significant in any subgroup (p > .35). This robust null result challenges the prevailing technological-optimistic narrative. It suggests the theoretical link between digital tools and enhanced governance is either fundamentally misspecified or contextually dependent in ways current theories do not capture. The research concludes that the impact of civic technology is not universal but is instead shaped by preexisting institutional capacity.

title: Socio-Cultural History of Elaziğ Mental Health and Neurological Diseases Hospital
affiliations: Mardin Artuklu Üniversitesi and Kocaeli University

detail.title: Socio-Cultural History of Elaziğ Mental Health and Neurological Diseases Hospital

declarations.ethicsApproval: Within the scope of the research, ethics committee approval numbered E.738266 was received from the Social and Human Sciences Ethics Committee of the Kocaeli University Presidency of the Republic of Turkey.

detail.abstract: This study examines the general course of Elazığ Mental and Nervous Diseases Hospital, examining its social transformations and circumstances. Founded in 1925 as an early modernization project of the Republic, the hospital functioned not only as a healthcare institution but also as a tool for the social and cultural community. Using a single descriptive case study, the research examines the hospital's traditional journey through three periods: the founding period (1925-1950), the institutionalization period (1950-1980), and the neoliberal transformation period (1980-present). Five main themes emerged from the analysis of participants' institutional reports during the interviews: the emergence of institutional personality as personal, the shift in social perceptions and stigmatization, the sociocultural dimensions of treatment practices, body-power relations, and class-gender dynamics. The findings demonstrate that social modernization occurred at the micro-level during the hospital's transition from the Ottoman Empire to the Republic. Perceptions of mental health problems evolved from religious and spiritual explanations to a treatment paradigm, and from fear to understanding. Western-derived psychiatric knowledge, local cultural debates, and hybrid treatment solutions are presented. The hospital, as an order, is both a disciplinary regime and an order of resistance, drawing on Foucault's biopower and Goffman's total institutions framework. Categories of social inequality, such as class, gender, and ethnic identity, significantly characterize treatment options and the treatment experience. This research reveals that mental health is not only a treatment issue but also a social, cultural, and political issue. The findings emphasize that thermotherapy is considered alongside medical treatments in the development of mental health policies.

title: Does Competition from For-Profit Firms Raise Wages for Preschool Workers?
affiliations: Stockholm University and Research Institute of Industrial Economics (IFN)

detail.title: Does Competition from For-Profit Firms Raise Wages for Preschool Workers?

declarations.ethicsApproval: The project has been approved by the Swedish Ethical Review Authority (Dnr 2020-04676).
declarations.funderStatement: This project has received funding from the Swedish Research Council, Dnr 2018-04714.

publicationDetails.journalName: Research Institute of Industrial Economics (IFN) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study the wage effects of an expansion of for-profit preschools in Sweden, which followed after a reform in 2006 removed municipalities' right to veto private entry. The expansion decreased preschool employers' monopsony power by increasing the number of alternative employers. We use a differences-indifferences event study design to evaluate the impact on preschool workers' wages, and find no evidence that wages were affected. In the context that we study, the absence of an upward wage effect may be explained by the entering for-profit firms' propensity to hire less qualified, lower-paid staff, and workers from other sectors of the economy than the preschool sector.

title: Spatial Reflection of Mental Health: A Sociological Study of Bakırköy Mental and Nervous Diseases Hospital
affiliations: Mardin Artuklu Üniversitesi

detail.title: Spatial Reflection of Mental Health: A Sociological Study of Bakırköy Mental and Nervous Diseases Hospital

declarations.ethicsApproval: The article was prepared in accordance with research and publication ethics. The necessary ethics committee approval for this study was obtained from the Munzur University Non-Interventional Research Ethics Committee at its 14th session held on December 31, 2020.

keywords: Bakirköy Mental Health and Neurological Diseases Training and Research Hospital

detail.abstract: This study investigates the social and spatial dimensions of mental health settings, specifically at the Bakırköy Mental Health and Neurological Diseases Training and Research Hospital. The aim of the research is to understand how the hospital setting is transformed into a living space and acquires social significance through the experiences and perspectives of healthcare workers. The research was conducted using a phenomenological design. The sample consisted of 10 participants, including nurses, medical secretaries, healthcare personnel, psychiatrists, and social workers. The sample was selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected using a semi-structured interview form developed by the researchers. The content and details of the interviews were analyzed using content analysis with the MAXQDA program. The study emphasizes that mental health spaces are complex and contain numerous stories. It also highlights the importance of a sociological perspective in hospitals, where mental health and spaces are in constant interaction.

title: Decentralised Science (DeSci): Transforming Research Funding with Blockchain Technology
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Decentralised Science (DeSci): Transforming Research Funding with Blockchain Technology
detail.abstract: The conventional research funding systems have been typified by systemic inefficiency such as bottlenecks in bureaucracy, allocation of resources to the already known researchers, and poor transparency in the peer review process. The current paper will discuss the ways in which Decentralised Science (DeSci) uses the blockchain technology and Decentralised Autonomous Organisations (DAOs) to provide solutions to these issues and democratise the research funding process. DeSci provides community-driven funding, leads researcher-to-community interactions, and new incentives like quadratic funding and Intellectual Property Non-Fungible Tokens (IP-NFTs) through immutable, transparent ledger systems. The paradigm supports global collaboration, removes intermediaries and rewards reproducibility and serious peer review by use of token-based reward systems. Regardless of the perceived benefits, such as increased transparency and inclusivity, institutional capacity to manage digital assets and uneven regulatory frameworks between jurisdictions are only a few of the roadblocks to widespread adoption. This research paper concludes that despite ongoing technical and legal issues, DeSci is a disruptive way of financing research, capable of speeding up scientific breakthroughs, especially when projects and studies with high risk, high-reward are concerned and those that deal with marginalised communities. The article recommends initiating more researcher interest in DeSci platforms and suggests that universities and grant providers should work together to build the right infrastructure and governance systems.

title: How Men and Women Respond to Failure: Evidence from Chess Tournaments
affiliations: Kiel University

detail.title: How Men and Women Respond to Failure: Evidence from Chess Tournaments
detail.abstract: Setbacks are inevitable in professional life, yet we know little about how people respond to them. I study how men and women respond to failure in a highly competitive setting, using 286,140 games from 3,523 titled chess players in a weekly tournament series. The weekly, 11round structure and fixed player pool allow me to track both short-and long-term responses to losses. After a loss, men play less accurately, choose riskier openings, and are more likely to quit the tournament. In contrast, women maintain or improve their performance, showing greater resilience. Over the long run, however, men and women are equally likely to reenter tournaments and invest in skill development, conditional on past outcomes. These findings suggest that short-term emotional responses differ by gender, but longer-term competitive choices are primarily skill-and success-driven.

title: Utilization Pattern of Paddy Residue Management Techniques (PRMT) by Paddy Farmers in Eluru District, Andhra Pradesh
affiliations: Agricultural College,, Agricultural College,, Agricultural College, and Agricultural College,

detail.title: Utilization Pattern of Paddy Residue Management Techniques (PRMT) by Paddy Farmers in Eluru District, Andhra Pradesh
detail.abstract: The utilization pattern of PRMT by paddy farmers was studied in Eluru district of Andhra Pradesh, which was purposively selected due to its significant contribution to paddy cultivation and residue generation. The study was conducted from oct 2024 to june 2025 to understand the adoption levels and improve sustainable residue management practices. Three mandals viz. Bhimadolu, Denduluru, and Pedapadu were selected randomly, and a total of 120 farmers were selected using a simple random sampling technique. The results revealed that little more than three-fifths (61.66%) of the paddy farmers had the medium utilization pattern followed by low (20.83%) and high (17.51%) utilization pattern of PRMT. Traditional techniques emerged as the most prominent, secured the highest index score of 73.40 followed by field techniques ranked second with a score of 62.26, whereas recent interventions ranked third with an index score of 56.94 and industrial techniques with a score of 49.65 claimed the fourth position. The study aims to assess the utilization patterns and management strategies of paddy residue adopted by farmers to ensure effective policy formulation, strengthen extension strategies and encourage environmentally sustainable practices that enhance both agricultural productivity and resource conservation. It provides insights on the factors that facilitate and hinder the adoption of PRMT, bridging the gap between environmental sustainability goals and grassroots agriculture practices.

title: Towards a Unified Model of Science Park
affiliations: Kingston University - School of Computer Science and Mathematics and Kingston University

detail.title: Towards a Unified Model of Science Park
detail.abstract: Science and Technology Parks (STPs) encourage small innovative start-ups and thus are seen to contribute to regional development. As the STP grows, poor decisions will scale accordingly and become more costly, eventually leading to STP market failure or a forced re-orientation of the organization to e.g. general business hosting. However correct decision-making by the central STP entity can be strengthened by inclusion of experienced managers with relevant knowledge from larger firms.

title: The AfCFTA: Legal Challenges in Promoting Regional Integration and Trade Facilitation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The AfCFTA: Legal Challenges in Promoting Regional Integration and Trade Facilitation
detail.abstract: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) represents a monumental step toward regional integration and economic growth in Africa. However, its successful implementation hinges on overcoming significant legal challenges. This article examines the legal obstacles hindering the AfCFTA’s objectives of trade facilitation and regional integration. It delves into issues such as inconsistencies between national and regional laws, tariffs and non-tariff barriers, customs procedures, and competition policies. By identifying these legal challenges, the article aims to contribute to effective solutions for overcoming and maximizing the AfCFTA’s potential benefits for African countries.

title: Motherhood and Labour Market Outcomes: Penalty or Premium?
affiliations: , University of Nevada, Reno and Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Bombay

detail.title: Motherhood and Labour Market Outcomes: Penalty or Premium?

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Using nationally representative longitudinal data from the Consumer Pyramids Household Survey, we examine the effect of childbirth on female labour market outcomes in India. Contrary to findings from similar studies in developed countries, we do not observe any motherhood penalty in earnings, employment or work hours post-childbirth, after accounting for unobserved individual heterogeneity. Interestingly, we find that the birth of a child leads to a 27.4% and 32.6% increase in womens average earnings in urban and rural regions, respectively, relative to non-mothers. This motherhood premium seems to arise partly due to higher employment after childbirth. Further, we find that the increase in the likelihood of employment is predominantly observed among women from lower caste, Hindu religion, lower income quartiles, those with primary education, and higher order births in urban regions. In rural regions, the effect is restricted to women from the lowest income quartiles. We find that the presence of older siblings in the household increases the likelihood of womens employment by 3.7 percentage points. These findings underscore the role of socio-economic factors in shaping the labour market outcomes of women in India.

title: Investigating the Effect of the Israel-Palestine Conflict on Jewish-Managed Companies in the S&P 500
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Investigating the Effect of the Israel-Palestine Conflict on Jewish-Managed Companies in the S&P 500
detail.abstract: This study examines whether the Israel-Palestine war of October 2023 had a measurable financial impact on Jewish-managed firms, using the event as an exogenous shock. A sample of 24 Jewish-managed firms from the S&P 500 was matched with 24 non-Jewish firms from the same industries, using Fama-French sector classifications and comparable business models. Paired sample t-tests were conducted on monthly stock returns for pre-and post-conflict periods to assess the significance of return differences. Firms were also categorized based on whether they made a public statement about the conflict, allowing for further subgroup analysis. Despite widespread media coverage and public backlash toward some corporate responses, the results showed no statistically significant differences in stock return patterns between Jewish-managed firms and their peers. Time series visualizations reinforced this, with most matched pairs tracking each other closely post-conflict. The findings suggest that investor behavior remained primarily driven by fundamentals rather than identity-based biases or political sentiment. While limitations include potential errors in identifying firm management and the use of monthly (rather than daily) returns, the study contributes to understanding how financial markets process geopolitical shocks. It also underscores the resilience of large, diversified firms to reputational and geopolitical events.

title: The Guardianship Dilemma: PLA Loyalty

detail.title: The Guardianship Dilemma: PLA Loyalty

declarations.ethicsApproval: All research in this paper was conducted in compliance with the ethical guidelines of the affiliated academic institutions (American University and School of Oriental & African Studies).

detail.abstract: The Guardianship Dilemma: PLA Loyalty Xi, as well as every prior Secretary General, in administering the PLA has encountered one core dilemma, a dilemma that remains both central to Xi's reforms and the role of the PLA as a militarized force. This 'Guardianship Dilemma' can be described as the tradeoff faced by autocratic regimes in which having a strong military can secure the regime from threats of internal unrest and foreign intervention, yet allows the military the resources and influence to challenge the central political authority. A weak military, though less effective at deterring threats, is easier to control and less likely to stage a coup. As described by political scientist Daniel C. Mattingly, "leaders must decide whether to build a strong coercive apparatus that can help them guard against mass threats but that poses a greater coup risk or a weak apparatus that will be less capable of launching a coup but also less capable of putting down mass threats". However, this is not the only dilemma faced by 1 Chinese leadership concerning the power of the PLA. A consequence of the Guardianship Dilemma, autocratic regimes tend to promote loyal generals for domestic threats, while favoring competent officers during foreign threats. For example, during the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests, Deng Xiaoping purged sympathetic leadership, replacing them with loyal officers to suppress unrest. On the contrary, the accidental US bombing of the Chinese embassy in Belgrade in 1999 represents a shift from domestic to foreign threat. Expectedly, at the time secretary Jiang Zemin substantially increased the PLA budget following a series of promotions offered to combat veteran officers, in response to rising fears of US hegemonism. However, Jiang Zemin's decision to maintain chairmanship over the CMC after his retirement limited his successor, Hu Jintao's, ability to appoint his own political allies within the PLA.

title: Temperature Variations and Domestic Violence

detail.title: Temperature Variations and Domestic Violence
detail.abstract: I combine detailed crime reports, independent helpline data, and high-frequency weather records to investigate how temperature variations influence domestic violence (DV) in Mexico City. I find a positive, contemporaneous, and linear relationship between daily temperature and DV, with a 1°C rise leading to a 2.8% increase in DV reports. This effect emerges even under moderate climatic conditions, suggesting continuous risk beyond extreme heat events. My findings rule out that changes in victims' reporting behavior entirely drive the relationship. Exploiting detailed census data from nearly 2,500 neighborhoods, I show that temperatureinduced DV disproportionately affects poorer areas, revealing how environmental stressors exacerbate existing urban inequalities.

title: Youth’s Potential of Adopting the Mediterranean Diet Lifestyle in Response to Climate Change: Empirical Study in Crete, Greece
affiliations: University of Nebraska at Lincoln, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, Pennsylvania State University and Mediterranean Agronomic Institute of Chania

detail.title: Youth’s Potential of Adopting the Mediterranean Diet Lifestyle in Response to Climate Change: Empirical Study in Crete, Greece
detail.abstract: The Mediterranean diet is considered one of the healthiest and most balanced dietary models currently in existence. Different studies suggest that it is environmentally friendly: it combines low greenhouse gas emissions, low demand for soil water, and less deforestation. Climate change can be mitigated through what consumers decide to eat. This article addresses the issue of by studying the intention of young consumers to shift their diets towards the Mediterranean Diet to prevent climate change through face interviews, collected in Crete, Greece (N=287). Using the Theory of Planned Behavior, the objective is to identify whether attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control guide such a behavior. Our findings highlight that young consumers’ perceived behavioral control has the highest influence on the intention, followed by their attitudes. As for the subjective norms, it has no significant impact on the intention.

detail.abstract: Microbial communities of biological soil crusts (biocrusts) are pivotal regulators of carbon and nutrient fluxes in vegetation-poor ecosystems. However, it remains poorly understood how environmental extremes impact the composition and functional properties of these microbiomes. Here, we combined physicochemical analyses with 16S rRNA and ITS2 amplicon sequencing to determine the environmental controls on microbial community composition and functionality across four Chilean biocrust sites with extreme conditions ranging from the hyper-arid, saline-alkaline Atacama Desert to the cold, acidic, Al-rich soils of subantarctic Patagonia. Site effects explained 75% and 63% of bacterial and fungal βdiversity, respectively, consistent with a strong site-specific pedoclimatic context. Among measured variables, pH, Na⁺, C, Al, and related soil nutrients (K⁺, Mg²⁺, N, Olsen-P) were associated with community patterns. We detected a cosmopolitan core of 100 bacterial and 42 fungal ASVs (dominated by Actinobacteriota/Proteobacteria and Ascomycota, respectively) nested within large site-exclusive halos (up to 552 bacterial ASVs), evidencing concurrent functional redundancy and biogeographic endemism. Our analyses revealed two contrasting edaphic guilds: an "alkaline-saline/osmotolerant" consortium versus an "acidorganic/Al-tolerant" consortium. Functional inference (FAPROTAX, FungalTraits) showed aerobic chemoheterotrophy as the only ubiquitous function, whereas nitrogen fixation peaked in Atacama (12% of bacterial ASVs), and hydrocarbon degradation and methanol oxidation were enriched in the Patagonian crusts. Fungal guilds shifted from lichen parasites and biotrophs in the desert to saprotrophs and ectomycorrhizal taxa in Patagonia. We conclude that there is limited functional convergence across extreme environments and highlight a need for site-tailored, genome-informed synthetic communities to leverage biocrust microorganisms in soil recarbonisation and restoration strategies.

detail.abstract:
This study evaluates the performance of the Parabolic Stop and Reverse (SAR) indicator when applied to Bitcoin (BTC/USDT), using both hourly (1H) and daily (1D) timeframes. Three execution modes were tested—BUYONLY, SELLONLY, and BOTH (long–short reversal)—and their performance was compared to a BTC Buy & Hold benchmark under zero transaction costs.

The results show that the standalone Parabolic SAR performs poorly in continuous trading conditions. While the BUYONLY model captures portions of major bullish cycles, it suffers from deep drawdowns and unstable equity behaviour. The SELLONLY mode performs extremely poorly due to Bitcoin’s structural upward trend, and the BOTH mode collapses under frequent whipsaws generated by SAR’s reactive nature.

However, the study also investigates a calibrated version of SAR that trades only during statistically profitable windows (Monday, Wednesday, Friday between 15:00–19:00 UTC). This calibrated BUYONLY model significantly improves risk-adjusted performance, achieving a Sharpe ratio of 1.35 and a Calmar ratio of 0.86, with substantially reduced volatility and drawdowns.

Overall, the findings confirm that Parabolic SAR requires contextual filters—such as time-of-day constraints, trend confirmation, or volatility regimes—to achieve sustainable profitability in cryptocurrency markets. As a continuous standalone system, SAR is unstable, but when selectively applied during structurally favourable periods, it becomes a viable and risk-efficient trend-following approach.

detail.title: Grit Mediates Social Success Across Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Tendencies
detail.abstract: Background: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) can erode social and occupational functioning. Grit—the perseverance and passion toward long-term goals—has been linked to favorable life outcomes. We examined whether grit mediates the association between ADHD tendencies and social success, operationalized as monthly income.Methods: We conducted an online survey of 2,321 adults in Japan. ADHD tendencies were assessed with the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS; Inattention and Hyperactivity). Grit was measured with the 12-item Japanese Grit Scale (Perseverance of Effort, Consistency of Interest). Self-reported monthly income indexed economic success. Standardized multiple regression and bootstrap mediation tested direct and indirect effects; a parallel mediation model evaluated the grit subcomponents simultaneously.Results: The total ADHD score was inversely related to grit (β = −0.049, p < .001) but not to income (β = −0.002, p = .868). Hyperactivity associated lower income (β = −0.015, p = .016), whereas Inattention did not (β = 0.001, p = .881). Mediation analysis showed that grit fully mediated the association between ADHD tendencies and income (indirect effect p < .001; direct effect p = .847). In parallel mediation, the pathway was driven by Perseverance of Effort (p < .001), while Consistency of Interest was not significant (p = .231).Conclusions: Grit—specifically perseverance of effort—emerged as a key mechanism linking ADHD tendencies with diminished earnings, offsetting a direct association. Because grit is cultivatable, interventions that strengthen sustained effort may mitigate economic disadvantage among adults with elevated ADHD tendencies and represent a pragmatic target for functional improvement.

detail.abstract:
India’s agriculture reliant rural economy has been inordinately exposed to climate change and subsequent risks forever. Erratic rainfall, heatwaves, droughts, and floods have intensified over the past decade, with direct repercussions for rural livelihoods and credit performance. According to the Economic Survey 2023–24, India witnessed a 28% increase in extreme weather events affecting agricultural output across 320 districts in the past five years.i These disruptions ripple through rural lending portfolios, thereby contributing to loan delinquencies, impaired asset values, and rising Non-Performing Assets (NPAs).

Financial institutions, especially Public Sector Banks (PSBs), Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), and cooperative credit institutions, are mandated under RBI’s PSL framework to allocate 40% of their Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) to priority sectors, with 18% earmarked for agriculture.iiThe current PSL structure, however, does not fully incorporate climate susceptibility. Meanwhile, sustainability-linked regulations like SEBI’s Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) mandate banks to disclose ESG exposures, adding pressure for environmentally responsible lending.

Artificial Intelligence, with its capacity to scrutinize massive, multi-source datasets and uncover non-linear risk patterns, offers a resilient solution. AI can distinguish apparent climate trends, quantify regional risks, and bear the design of mantic, adaptive credit models that fall in line with both PSL and ESG objectives.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines the constitutional, legal, and moral consequences of President Donald Trump’s 2025 military operations in the Caribbean, which were justified under the doctrine of “necessity.” It argues that these actions—conducted without congressional authorization and beyond recognized international law—constituted a deliberate experiment in constitutional endurance. The strikes against alleged Venezuelan “narcoterrorist” vessels were not isolated acts of foreign policy but a calculated test of how far executive power could exceed legal limits without provoking resistance.

Drawing upon constitutional history, judicial precedent, and political philosophy, the paper situates this experiment within the long evolution of executive overreach—from Truman’s Korea to Obama’s drone wars—and identifies Trump’s contribution as the conversion of secrecy into spectacle. The War Powers Resolution, designed to restrain unilateral action, was transformed into a ceremonial formality. Congress’s silence and the courts’ procedural abstention together signaled not balance but abdication. What began as emergency justification evolved into a doctrine of perpetual authority, legitimized by public apathy and institutional fatigue.

The study also traces how imperial power abroad metastasized into domestic governance. The same logic that sanctioned extralegal force overseas—loyalty rhetoric, moral necessity, and administrative discretion—returned home in the language of “law and order.” The erosion of limits thus became psychological as much as legal. Citizens accustomed to permanent warfare began to conflate obedience with patriotism, mistaking command for order.

Ultimately, the paper concludes that the Republic’s collapse will not come through rebellion but through normalization. The Constitution remains intact in form but hollow in function, sustained by rituals of legality that conceal the decay of accountability. The “edge of the Republic” is not a geographic frontier but a moral threshold—the point at which a people forget that freedom requires vigilance, and that silence, repeated long enough, becomes consent.

detail.abstract:
Housing courts need a renovation. Referred to more commonly as “eviction courts,” they have gone from a forum where tenants and landlords resolve lease and habitability disputes to a graveyard for housing security. In non-payment proceedings, during which landlords seek to recover unpaid rent, the lack of remedies available to low-income tenants makes evictions a certainty. Evictions should be removed as a possible result for non-payment of rent. When an eviction happens because of a non-payment proceeding, both the landlord and tenant lose. The landlord loses litigation costs and any ability to recuperate the rent owed, but the tenant loses more — the stability and security that a home provides. Evictions also put a strain on the resources local governments use to support low-income households. Repudiating evictions as a resolution for these proceedings would allow for equitable solutions for all parties to materialize.

This Article narrows in on the inequity of non-payment proceedings by focusing on the displacement of low-income households. It analyzes the intended role of evictions through the progression of housing courts into eviction courts. It then examines the harm evictions pose for all litigants and their communities. It subsequently explores the scholarly interest in housing court reform, most of which suggests innovative methods to reduce evictions. This Article contends that even with these innovations, evictions have an unfair impact on poor tenants of color. It concludes that the most straightforward way to reduce evictions is to remove them as a result of nonpayment proceedings in housing court.

detail.abstract:
The collapse of constitutional loyalty in the contemporary United States does not announce itself through rebellion or revolution, but through the quiet normalization of obedience. This paper examines the structural erosion of the constitutional oath—from a living act of civic responsibility into a ritual of institutional conformity. Drawing upon the framework established in Hadric Rowe’s preceding works, Vengeance and the Erosion of Constitutional Order and Guardians of the Constitution, the study situates the 2025 Caribbean military strikes authorized by President Donald Trump as a paradigmatic case of executive overreach cloaked in legality. Through these events, the article demonstrates how the executive branch, invoking “national security” and “armed conflict with drug cartels,” has unilaterally expanded the war powers of the presidency, bypassed congressional authorization, and reduced the judiciary to a posture of restraint. 

The analysis proceeds through the constitutional, institutional, and philosophical dimensions of this crisis. Constitutionally, the strikes defy Article I, Section 8, which vests the power to declare war in Congress. Institutionally, the silence of Congress, the military’s uncritical compliance, and the Supreme Court’s reliance on the “political question” doctrine have collectively transformed separation of powers into an appearance rather than a practice. Philosophically, this erosion reveals the transmutation of loyalty from duty to deference, from moral responsibility to administrative obedience. The paper argues that such transformation represents not a temporary deviation but a redefinition of the republic’s moral order.

 Employing primary legal texts, judicial precedents—including Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer, 343 U.S. 579 (1952)—and classical sources from The Federalist Papers and Montesquieu’s The Spirit of the Laws, the article contends that constitutional fidelity cannot survive without procedural vigilance. When presidential command supplants lawful authorization, when legality is manufactured through classified opinions, and when citizens internalize indifference as normalcy, the Constitution ceases to govern in fact though it remains in form. The greatest danger to a constitutional democracy, therefore, is not the usurpation of power but the quiet consent that follows it—the moment when the oath endures as ceremony while its meaning has already died.

detail.abstract: The article examines the foundational principles of biomedical ethics and their relevance to the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) and biotechnological progress. It then analyzes the potential impact of the National Institutes of Health's (NIH or the Agency) proposed 2024 reorganization reforms, as presented by the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (E&C), and advocates for the inclusion of provisions that would enable the Agency to develop and deploy "safe, secure, and trustworthy" AI within the biotechnology sector. Thus, the article proposes two key integrative reforms to address these concerns: (1) enhancing research collaborations among healthcare systems, academic institutions, and the private sector through AI-driven platforms, and (2) establishing an NIH office to oversee AI-based health initiatives. These reforms would require legislative amendments, including updates to the Patent and Trademark Law Amendments Act of 1980 (Bayh-Dole Act or Bayh Dole) and the 21st Century Cures Act of 2016 (Cures Act), while adhering to biomedical ethics. Such amendments would ensure (1) ethical standards in collaborative research and development (R&D) among institutions and (2) effective health initiative design and implementation. In the same light, this article advocates for an updated legislative framework to the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) that regulates the role of such integrative efforts and balances the transformative potential of AI in biotechnology. In all, these regulatory steps ensure that innovation benefits society while safeguarding individual rights such as personal data and privacy and mitigating algorithmic bias.
