This paper examines the constitutional and ethical implications of the Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education, a 2025 initiative of the Trump administration that sought to condition federal funding on universities’ adherence to specific ideological standards. By analyzing the text of the compact, institutional responses, and constitutional doctrine, the study argues that the initiative represents an unprecedented expansion of executive power through fiscal coercion—transforming delegated budgetary authority into an instrument of ideological enforcement.

The paper situates the compact within the broader process of constitutional self-erosion, in which legality is weaponized to undermine liberty. Drawing on Train v. City of New York (1975), South Dakota v. Dole (1987), and Keyishian v. Board of Regents (1967), it demonstrates that the executive’s manipulation of public finance violates the spirit of the Spending Clause and the substantive guarantees of the First Amendment. Universities such as MIT, Brown, Penn, and USC rejected the compact not as political protest but as constitutional fidelity, preserving the principle that truth and academic freedom cannot be purchased.

The analysis further explores the cultural dimension of erosion—the normalization of dependency and the moral fatigue of the public. Fiscal coercion, disguised as administrative reform, replaces consent with submission and transforms neutrality into silence. The resulting “administrative autocracy” redefines executive power as managerial authority over civic life, while the people’s indifference accelerates constitutional decay.

Ultimately, the paper contends that the collapse of constitutional power begins not with decrees but with the quiet acceptance of conditional obedience. The restoration of republican integrity requires the revival of civic conscience and the reaffirmation of fiduciary government—the recognition that public funds are held in trust, not wielded as instruments of control. The defense of constitutional freedom, therefore, begins with the courage to refuse unlawful offers, even when silence promises comfort.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the constitutional, ethical, and political dimensions of the emerging retaliatory state in the United States—a regime in which the instruments of law are repurposed as instruments of vengeance. Through the lens of the indictments of John Bolton, James Comey, and Letitia James, the study argues that political retaliation has evolved from an aberration into a structural pathology, eroding both institutional independence and civic trust. The analysis traces this transformation across ten chapters: from the philosophical warnings of the Founders to the moral inversion that rewards cruelty over restraint. The paper contends that the American constitutional system, though designed to balance ambition, is ill-equipped to resist sustained retribution from within. Once the executive branch normalizes vengeance through judicial means, the separation of powers becomes a façade, and constitutional governance devolves into a competition of punishments. Drawing on United States v. Nixon, Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer, Hartman v. Moore, and relevant scholarly commentary, the argument situates this crisis within the broader history of republics that collapsed under the weight of their own legality. The work proposes a four-stage model of constitutional decay—legalized retaliation, politicized justice, trust erosion, and institutional hollowing—culminating in what it calls the constitutional simulacrum, a republic that retains the appearance of democracy but loses its ethical substance. Ultimately, the paper issues a moral call to resistance: that citizens, legislators, and institutions must reject the normalization of political retribution before the Constitution becomes a parchment relic of forgotten faith.

detail.title: Strategic hiding and exploration in networks ​
detail.abstract: We propose and study a model of strategic network design and exploration where the hider, subject to a budget constraint restricting the number of links, chooses a connected network and the location of an object. Meanwhile, the seeker, not observing the network and the location of the object, chooses a network exploration strategy starting at a fixed node in the network. The network exploration follows the expanding search paradigm of Alpern and Lidbetter (2013). We obtain a Nash equilibrium and characterize equilibrium payoffs in the case of linking budget allowing for trees only. We also give an upper bound on the expected number of steps needed to find the hider for the case where the linking budget allows for at most one cycle in the network. ​

detail.abstract: With the growing awareness of the ecological environment, green finance plays an irreplaceable role in the process of sustainable development of productivity. Our work aims to investigate the efficiency of work coordination among various sectors of the economic system. By using kernel density estimation and the Markov chain model, this study constructs a coupled coordination model among government, society, and financial institutions from the perspective of green finance. It explores the spatio-temporal evolution of the degree of coupled coordination in 31 Chinese provinces and regions. Besides, by using a two-way fixed-effects model and analyzing regional heterogeneity, this context also explores the role of the degree of coupling coordination among various sectors of the economic system on economic and social development based on the perspective of green finance. The empirical results show that: (1) The coupling coordination degree across provinces has shown an overall upward trend year by year. The four major economic regions exhibit a clear pattern of synchronous development, although regional disparities have gradually widened. Specifically, the eastern region maintains the highest average coupling coordination degree, while the western region demonstrates significant polarization. (2) In the short term, China's provinces display a "club convergence" effect in their coupling coordination degrees, predominantly clustering at intermediate levels and maintaining this status quo. However, from a long term perspective, an upward trend is anticipated. (3) By improving the level of new quality productive forces and digital economy levels in the provinces, the coupling coordination degree can significantly facilitate the process of quality improvement and efficiency enhancement. These findings hold substantial implications for fostering green finance coordination among different regions from governmental, societal, and financial institutional perspectives.

title: The Consolidation Paradox in Labor Markets: Network Fragility and Spatial Wage Spillovers
affiliations: University of Tokyo

detail.title: The Consolidation Paradox in Labor Markets: Network Fragility and Spatial Wage Spillovers
detail.abstract:
Existing spatial econometrics cannot answer basic questions about minimum wage spillovers: How far do effects reach? Through what channels? This paper derives spatial treatment effects from first principles using Navier-Stokes partial differential equations, yielding three key discoveries. First, wage spillovers exhibit self-similar scaling: treatment boundaries grow as √ t following universal diffusion laws, not adhoc assumptions. Empirical validation confirms the theoretical prediction exactly (β = 0.500, R 2 = 1.00). Second, Modified Bessel K0 functions provide the correct spatial weights, fitting data three times better than alternatives commonly used in applied work (R 2 = 0.99 vs. 0.35 for exponential decay). Third, network consolidation increases rather than dampens wage volatility during stress periods—a ”consolidation paradox” that intensified post-COVID-19, with consolidation-volatility correlation rising from near-zero to +0.0067.
Using 64,421 county-quarter observations (2018-2023), I estimate characteristic spillover distance of 100 miles with effects building cumulatively to 0.44 log points over four quarters. Economic networks dominate geographic proximity 8:1, indicating that who you’re connected to matters more than where you are. Spatial decay parameters increased 27% during COVID-19 (from κ = 0.0155 to 0.0196), shrinking effective spillover radius from 65 to 51 miles—validating time-varying dynamics predicted by perturbation theory.
These findings provide concrete policy guidance. For the United States, regional minimum wage policies should coordinate within 100-mile radius under normal conditions, contracting to 65 miles during crises. For Japan’s aggressive minimum wage reform (targeting 1,500 yen/hour by 2030, up 50% from current levels), the framework predicts Tokyo’s increases will substantially affect surrounding prefectures (Kanagawa, Saitama, Chiba) within 160 kilometers, while distant prefectures (Tohoku, Kansai) require independent adjustments. Network consolidation analysis reveals Tokyo’s concentrated labor market structure amplifies shocks, requiring gradual phase-ins, while diversified rural prefectures can absorb discrete increases. The self-similar scaling property—where boundaries evolve as t 1/2 regardless of threshold—implies spillovers reach 50% of final extent within one year but continue expanding indefinitely, making multi-year policy coordination essential.

detail.abstract:
This study examines the progressive erosion of constitutional equilibrium in the United States through the transformation of political loyalty into an organizing principle of governance. What began as a struggle for influence within a single political party—through endorsements, threats, and purges—has evolved into a systemic redefinition of constitutional order. The separation of powers, though preserved in text, has been emptied of substance. Legislative independence has withered under the administrative shadow; judicial restraint has yielded to political alignment; and public deliberation has dissolved into partisan obedience. The institutional form of democracy remains intact, yet its animating virtues—responsibility, moderation, and accountability—have receded into ritual. Under Article I of the Constitution, Congress was designed to embody the people’s will, independent of executive coercion. In contemporary practice, however, the legislature functions as a derivative organ—bound not by law, but by the economic and rhetorical gravity of the presidency. The rise of administrative party-building, in which the executive simultaneously acts as movement, propaganda apparatus, and disciplinary authority, has blurred the boundary between governance and allegiance. The logic of loyalty now supplants the logic of legality. Madison’s dictum in The Federalist No. 51—that “ambition must be made to counteract ambition”—has been inverted; ambition now consolidates rather than counterbalances. The republican mechanism remains, but its direction is reversed. 

The abuse of presidential clemency illustrates this deeper transformation. Once conceived in Ex parte Garland, 71 U.S. 333 (1866), as an act of mercy aimed at reconciliation, the pardon has become a political currency through which loyalty is rewarded and dissent punished. This selective absolution erodes the due process guarantee of the Fifth Amendment and converts equality before the law into a conditional privilege. Detached from justice, mercy becomes an instrument of control. The legal system retains its ceremonial form but loses its moral coherence. The decay is not the suspension of law but its instrumentalization—a subtler form of constitutional collapse operating behind a façade of legality. 

The same inversion appears in the state’s control of information and secrecy. Under the banners of “national security” and “executive privilege,” transparency is withheld not to protect the republic, but to shield the executive from accountability. In Locke’s theory of prerogative, the executive may act beyond the law only for the public good; yet when prerogative becomes habitual, it ceases to be an exception and becomes a method of rule. The concealment of public records—particularly where official misconduct is implicated—reveals how the informational architecture of democracy has been repurposed. Knowledge, once the foundation of citizenship, is now monopolized as an instrument of governance. Concurrently, political language has undergone moral degradation. The vocabulary that once mediated between principle and policy has devolved into the rhetoric of denunciation. The constitutional lexicon—rights, duties, equality, justice—has been replaced by the vernacular of loyalty and betrayal. This linguistic decay is not superficial; it signifies the disappearance of the civic ethos sustaining constitutional restraint. As Hannah Arendt observed, the corruption of language precedes the corrosion of freedom. When law ceases to speak in a vocabulary of reason, it survives only as command. The digital age magnifies this process. Social media transforms politics into performance, citizens into algorithmic subjects, and consent into spectacle. Participation has been simulated through engagement metrics, giving rise to digital authoritarianism—a participatory autocracy where the crowd echoes rather than constrains power. The digital multitude mirrors the executive will; public discourse becomes the amplification of authority. Sovereignty thus migrates from the people to the system that interprets them. The argument advanced herein is not that the Constitution has been overthrown, but that it has been repurposed.

detail.abstract:
On October 15, 2025, dozens of Pentagon correspondents returned their badges rather than
sign a department policy conditioning access and inquiry on prior approval by the Secretary
of Defense. This paper argues that the episode constitutes a modern stress test of the First
Amendment and a constitutional event in its own right. The question is not merely whether
particular rules were overbroad, but whether executive power may transform the freedom to
ask and report into a licensed privilege. Drawing on the prior restraint line from Near v.
Minnesota to the Pentagon Papers decision, as well as separation-of-powers doctrine from
Youngstown and subsequent national-security cases, the analysis situates the Pentagon’s
policy within a broader, systematic attempt to regulate information flow under the banner of
security.
Methodologically, the paper relies on contemporaneous public records, newsroom
statements, and established constitutional doctrine. It proposes a normative framework—the
Doctrine of Constitutional Responsibility—under which constitutional vitality depends on
the willing exercise of institutional and civic duties when formal checks hesitate. Even if the
policy is rescinded and access restored, the constitutional meaning of October 15 endures: the
episode revealed the outer limits of executive discretion and reaffirmed the press as an
institutional safeguard rather than a partisan actor. In short, the press badges surrendered that
afternoon function less as revoked credentials than as emblems of constitutional service.

detail.abstract:
The endurance of the United States Constitution rests not on its textual permanence but on
its ethical architecture—an internal equilibrium between faith and restraint. This study situates
the Constitution as a moral and institutional design rather than a static document of authority. It
argues that constitutional stability derives from the reciprocal limitation of power and
conscience, in which institutional mechanisms function as moral instruments. Through a
combined analysis of constitutional text, Supreme Court jurisprudence, and classical political
theory, the paper identifies three intersecting lines of inquiry: the ethical logic of separation of
powers, the procedural defense of liberty, and the civic obligation of self-restraint. Drawing upon
The Federalist Papers, Locke’s Second Treatise of Government, and Montesquieu’s Spirit of the
Laws, it demonstrates how the American framers translated moral anthropology into institutional
design.
In the contemporary era—marked by executive overreach, congressional erosion, and
judicial politicization—the paper revisits the founding logic of limitation as an ethical remedy.
The study concludes that constitutional repair requires not only legal reform but a moral
reawakening of restraint within both government and citizenry

title: Water Quality in Indonesia: The Role of Socioeconomic Indicators

detail.title: Water Quality in Indonesia: The Role of Socioeconomic Indicators
detail.abstract: Population growth and the construction of settlements and industrial estates continue to increase at an unprecedented rate that has created gains and losses on environmental quality. The trend of population growth shows a declining trend but is not directly proportional to the fluctuating water quality index over the past ten years. The study uses secondary data with the quantitative approach using the panel data Fixed Effect Model (FEM) with Generalized Least Squares (GLS) to examine socioeconomic indicators in 34 provinces on water quality in Indonesia. Through analysis in this study shows that explanatory variables of the number of population and population density have a negative and significant effect on water quality in Indonesia of 4.69 and 1.95-ceteris paribus. The control variables of the number of establishments of micro and small scale manufacturing industry, and a group of workers, GRDP per capita, and realization of foreign direct investment show negative and significant results on water quality in Indonesia. It indicates that environmental management in Indonesia experiences a higher pressure from the utilization of ecological resources compared to efforts to improve the environment itself. Whereas household control variables of households and improve sanitation, the volume of water distributed by water supply establishment and the squared of GRDP per capita show positive and significant results on water quality in Indonesia, which shows that this is evidence of the government's success in managing the environment better.

detail.abstract: We introduce Authority Entropy, an index that quantifies the distribution of authority stances within dialogue windows and tests its predictive value for compliance, convergence speed, and equilibrium stability. Using a multilingual lexicon of authority-bearing constructions anchored in the regla compilada as an operational constraint set, we train a strictly causal classifier that maps text to stance probabilities over {low, neutral, high}. Authority Entropy is computed per sliding window, together with its slope and volatility, and related to behavioral endpoints through survival models and doubly robust estimators. The study spans synthetic arenas with controllable payoffs, open multi-party tasks with outcome labels, and consented human–model interactions. Baselines include sentiment, toxicity, politeness, formality, and power taggers. Stress tests apply adversarial edits that alter authority cues while preserving semantics to assess sensitivity of entropy and downstream effects. Primary outcomes are compliance rate, convergence time, payoff stability, and regret, reported with leakage audits, calibration checks, and confidence intervals. Results target a public specification of the index, a causal benchmark and leaderboard, and open tooling to visualize instability regimes over time. The contribution is a portable, language-aware measure that links local authority structure to cooperative dynamics without right context leakage.

title: Loving or Fighting Inflation: Optimal Policy in High-and Low-Debt Economies

detail.title: Loving or Fighting Inflation: Optimal Policy in High-and Low-Debt Economies
detail.abstract: The rise in public debt after the COVID-19 pandemic and the energy crisis has renewed debate over how fiscal and monetary policies should coordinate in highly indebted economies. We study optimal fiscal and monetary policy in high-and low-debt environments, using the United Kingdom in 2007 and 2021 as benchmarks. Within a heterogeneous-agent Ramsey framework with incomplete markets, we analyze how taxation, public debt, and inflation adjust following fiscal and productivity shocks. Higher public debt limits fiscal space, requiring sharper and more front-loaded tax adjustments and shifting the burden of stabilization toward monetary policy. When fiscal tools are constrained, moderate inflation becomes an endogenous and welfare-improving adjustment mechanism, reducing the real value of debt and smoothing consumption.

title: Gold, Drugs, Blood and Global Capital: The New Business Imperialism and Extractivism dynamics in Postcolonial Peru

detail.title: Gold, Drugs, Blood and Global Capital: The New Business Imperialism and Extractivism dynamics in Postcolonial Peru
detail.abstract: This article examines how Peru's gold economy, at the intersection of licit and illicit circuits, has become a conduit for contemporary forms of business imperialism. Against a backdrop of rising global demand for gold and sustained capital inflows, both formal mining operations and illegal gold extraction have expanded rapidly in Peru-facilitated by weak institutional oversight, transnational corporate networks, and growing links with drug trafficking circuits. Drawing from the frameworks of extractive imperialism, informal empire, and "slow violence", the paper interrogates how multinational actors and global commodity chains reproduce historical patterns of asymmetrical accumulation, while externalizing environmental degradation, health crises, and systemic violence to the peripheral territories of Peru. Through a political economy lens grounded in Latin American structuralism and postcolonial theory, the study highlights the paradox of a country with persistent trade surpluses but chronic current account deficits-driven by low royalties, primary income outflows, and the enclave nature of its resource sector. By tracing the gold economy's integration with coca-based illicit economies and its reliance on mercury-intensive extraction methods, the paper exposes how imperial dynamics of extraction have morphed, rather than disappeared, in the postcolonial era. Ultimately, this case repositions Peru's contemporary gold boom within broader discussions on the business history of imperialism, suggesting that modern extractive regimes are less a rupture with colonial forms than their reconfiguration through financial globalization and deregulated capital flows.

The objective of this study is to analyse the governance, technological, and enforcement challenges, along with the feasibility and potential benefits associated with the consolidation of tax collection functions under the Balochistan Revenue Authority (BRA). A mixed-methods approach was employed to scrutinise tax agency consolidation in Balochistan. title: Calvo's "Probability Zombie" and the Specter of Machine Learning: On the "Predictionist" Fallacy in Modern Macroeconomics

detail.title: Calvo's "Probability Zombie" and the Specter of Machine Learning: On the "Predictionist" Fallacy in Modern Macroeconomics
detail.abstract: This paper argues that the enduring dominance of the Calvo (1983) pricing model within New Keynesian macroeconomics, despite its demonstrably unrealistic microfoundations, is a symptom of a deep-seated methodological pathology we term the "predictionist fallacy"—the prioritization of a model's predictive fit over its causal-realist explanatory power. We first place the Calvo model on a "historical tribunal," identifying it as a modern incarnation of the Ptolemaic tradition of "epicycles": an ad-hoc mathematical device created not to explain reality, but to "save" a flawed core paradigm. We then introduce the "specter" of machine learning, demonstrating that purely atheoretical algorithms, by their empirically superior predictive performance, logically invalidate any justification for theory-laden models that rests solely on their predictive ability. This confrontation compels a "rectification of names" for economic science, urging a return to its classical mission: not the hubristic prediction of a fundamentally uncertain future, but the vital task of providing deep, causal understanding of the logic of human action. We conclude that in the dawning "post-predictionist" era, where algorithms will dominate forecasting, it is the Austrian School, with its steadfast rejection of predictive pretense and its unwavering focus on praxeology, that is uniquely positioned for a necessary and profound intellectual revival. This paper is therefore not merely a critique of a single model, but a manifesto for the future of economic science itself.

title: A US Concession to Russia on Ukraine would Usher in a New World Order

detail.abstract: The August 15 summit in Alaska between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin ended without a peace deal, but it signaled a deeper shift in global power dynamics. detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of Korea's universal long-term care insurance (LTCI) system, implemented in 2008, on the labor market outcomes of family caregivers. We exploit multiple discontinuities in the LTCI benefit structure to estimate the benefits' effect on caregiver employment. Analyzing data from a nationally representative survey, we find that LTCI benefits significantly increase labor force participation among women but have no corresponding effect among men. Additionally, the benefits reduce women's likelihood of engaging in family caregiving as their primary activity. These findings highlight the crucial role of long-term care policies in shaping labor market outcomes for caregivers, with notable implications for the dynamics of women's labor supply.

detail.abstract: We study how survey-based measures of funding needs and availability influence the transmission of euro area monetary policy to investment. We first provide evidence that funding needs are primarily driven by fundamentals, while perceived funding availability captures financial conditions. Using these two measures, we assess how the effectiveness of monetary policy varies with fundamentals and financial conditions. Our results indicate that monetary policy is most effective when firms’ fundamentals are strong. In contrast, firms with favorable financial conditions exhibit a more muted investment response to monetary policy. By combining these two survey-based measures, we construct an indicator of financial constraints and show that financially constrained firms are more sensitive to monetary policy. These findings offer new light on the transmission of monetary policy to corporate investment, emphasizing not only the role of financial conditions, but also the importance of fundamentals, which are beyond the direct influence of central banks

detail.title: Individual risk preferences and natural disasters
detail.abstract: Using exogenous variation in exposure to the 1997 Indonesian forest fires and accompanying smoke clouds, we document persistent effects of exposure to such natural disasters on individual risk preferences. People who are more intensely exposed to the fires and subsequent air pollution exhibit lower risk aversion and the effects last even 10 years after exposure but ultimately die down and can no longer be measured 18 years after exposure. The effects seem to be more pronounced among women, younger cohorts, and individuals living in lower socio-economic conditions. While some of these results are in line with those found in previous studies, there are also significant differences, particularly when it comes to the persistence of these effects over time, which point to the fact that the type of natural disaster considered and other context-specific factors matter.

detail.abstract: We report results from a large-scale, laboratory-style experiment in which a Large Language Model (LLM)-represented by three versions of ChatGPT-3.5-turbo-makes decisions and forms beliefs about the behavior of other players in a one-shot Prisoner's Dilemma (PD). Variations in payoffs have negligible effects on model behavior, whereas the other dimensions shift cooperation rates and beliefs in directions consistent with classic findings from experiments with human subjects. We further find that decisions and beliefs are highly correlated. Regressions show that the LLM's responses are highly predictable.

detail.abstract: We estimate the carbon impact of Japan’s high-speed rail expansion using a city-year panel from 2000 to 2020. Rather than relying only on binary station openings, we model continuous network connectivity via market access and use two complementary designs: a staggered difference-in-differences around openings with spatial spillovers and a market-access specification identified by two-stage least squares. The instrument is a geography-driven least-cost-path network that mitigates endogeneity in infrastructure placement. Over two decades, CO$_2$ emissions in manufacturing, construction, and retail decline by 98.373 million tons, about 0.203 percent of national emissions in these sectors. By sector, manufacturing accounts for 85.886 million tons, retail for 11.417 million tons, and construction for 1.070 million tons. Valued at USD 50 per ton, the implied social benefit is USD 5.644 billion. Most abatement is associated with system-wide connectivity rather than local openings. Mechanism evidence indicates that market access raises activity yet lowers carbon intensity, consistent with reallocation toward less energy-intensive production and process efficiency gains that dominate scale effects.

detail.abstract: Is there an undesired side-effect of banking regulation on the non-bank sector? Using a state-dependent local projection approach and a rich dataset capturing macroprudential tightening across euro area countries, we present strong cross-country heterogeneity. In financially conservative markets (Germany, France, the Netherlands), tight monetary policy combined with stricter macroprudential measures significantly contracts investment fund assets. Conversely, financial hubs (Luxembourg, Ireland, Italy) experience counterintuitive expansions under the same policy mix. Further disaggregation shows that equity funds are more vulnerable to joint tightening in conservative systems, while bond funds partly offset contractionary forces in hubs through higher yields.

detail.abstract: The 2008 global financial crisis marked the beginning of a decade dominated by fiscal austerity policies in much of the developed world. This paper presents a qualitative narrative review of an extensive collection of academic literature to synthesize evidence on the multifaceted effects of austerity. Following a thematic approach inspired by PRISMA guidelines, the economic, social, and political consequences of these measures are examined. The analysis reveals a majority consensus regarding the recessive effects of austerity, especially when implemented during economic crises, with negative fiscal multipliers that often exacerbate GDP contraction. Socially, austerity is associated with rising inequality, negative impacts on public health, disproportionate gender consequences, and a weakening of social safety nets. Politically, evidence links austerity to the erosion of trust in institutions, a rise in populism, and electoral instability. Despite the political narrative presenting austerity as an inevitable necessity for fiscal sustainability, academic literature underscores its high costs and questionable efficacy, advocating for more contextualized and equitable economic policy approaches.

detail.abstract: Background: Adult vaccination rates are consistently below national targets in the United States. A national survey was conducted to quantify and rank the relative importance of barriers to vaccination reported by a range of US healthcare professionals (HCPs), providing actionable insights for targeted intervention and policy efforts to improve adult vaccine uptake.Methods: A total of 1227 HCPs across office- and pharmacy-based settings participated in a quantitative survey in which barriers were ranked from a list of individual, interpersonal, community, and policy-level challenges following the Socio-Ecological Model. HCPs were defined as actively vaccinating clinicians and healthcare decision-makers. A MaxDiff (Best-Worst Scaling) analysis was performed to identify top barriers.Results: Interpersonal barriers, particularly patient hesitancy and vaccine refusal, were the most frequently cited challenges. Policy-level concerns, including reimbursement limitations and Medicare Part D complexities, emerged among primary care physicians and pharmacists. Community-level issues, such as staffing shortages, workflow constraints, and fragmented immunization records, were especially prominent for pharmacists and healthcare decision-makers. Individual-level concerns, including HCP reluctance to recommend vaccines or concerns about co-administration, were also reported.Conclusions: These findings highlight how adult vaccination is hindered by a complex, multilevel set of challenges. detail.abstract: This paper applies diagnostic expectations to analyze expectation formation in housing markets and uncovers a novel investment crowding-out mechanism. Using Korean housing market data, we find systematic overreaction—persistent optimism even as prices decline—that cannot be explained by rational expectations. Incorporating the diagnostic expectations proposed by Bordalo et al. (2018) into the housing DSGE model of Iacoviello (2005), we examine its macroeconomic spillover effects. When agents with a diagnosis bias overreact to positive housing market news—such as favorable preference shocks or expansionary monetary policy—they form excessively optimistic price expectations, fueling excessive housing demand, particularly among previously constrained agents, and diverting resources from productive investment. Consequently, overactivated expectations trigger an investment crowding-out effect in the productive sector. Unlike studies emphasizing bank lending channels, we show that expectation formation itself can misallocate resources. The results imply that effective housing policy should manage expectations through credible communication, and highlight the need for a coordination of monetary and macro-prudential policies.

detail.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has introduced powerful tools for reimagining how knowledge is produced, formalized, and validated. Large language models (LLMs), in particular, enable the articulation of complex ideas through natural language and the generation of outputs that resemble models, algorithms, or theoretical frameworks (Bender et al., 2021; Floridi and Chiriatti, 2020). While this capability has sparked interest in prompt engineering, existing approaches remain largely pragmatic, focusing on optimization heuristics rather than exploring the epistemological and methodological implications of prompts as instruments for theory-building (White et al., 2023). To address this gap, we introduce Prompt-Driven Conceptual Modeling (PDCM) as a systematic methodology that uses natural language prompts, mediated through generative AI, to produce structured conceptual artifacts. We further define Generative Theoretical Prototypes (GTPs) as provisional outputs of PDCM that serve as scaffolds for subsequent refinement and validation. Drawing from traditions of conceptual modeling (Booch, 1994; Object Management Group, nd), computational creativity (Colton and Wiggins, 2012; Boden, 2004), and design science research (Hevner et al., 2004), this paper argues that PDCM provides a reproducible framework for integrating human intuition, AI mediation, and scholarly rigor. Using case studies-spanning platform ecosystems, distributed computing architectures, and mathematical modeling-we illustrate how PDCM functions in practice. We conclude by positioning PDCM and GTP as contributions to both professional and academic education communities, identifying future directions for validation, benchmarking, and cross-disciplinary adoption.

detail.abstract: Worsening climatic conditions and water scarcity pose major threats to rural livelihoods and to the economic development of arid regions. This paper evaluates a large-scale, low-cost climate adaptation program that built one million rain-fed water storage cisterns in Brazils poorest and most drought-prone areas. Using novel individual-level administrative data and a difference-in-differences design, we show that the program substantially improved both economic and health outcomes, benefiting adults and children alike. Within ten years, household dependency on cash transfers fell by up to 34%, while formal labor income increased by 20%. Hospitalizations due to waterborne diseases declined by 16% among adults and 37% among children, and compliance with cash transfer conditionalities on child health and education improved. Additional evidence suggests that these gains were driven by a relaxation of time constraints: cisterns markedly reduced the time burden of water collection, enabling beneficiaries to allocate more time to productive activities. A cost-benefit analysis indicates a high marginal value of public funds relative to a broad range of public policies.

detail.abstract: This paper extends the theory of corporate insurance make-or-buy decisions to emerging markets with binding regulatory capital constraints, where discontinuous viability thresholds emerge from minimum capital requirements rather than traditional economies of scale. We develop a formal model where break-even points become step functions of regulatory parameters, investment returns, and medical trend rates, with comparative statics showing how capital requirements create discrete market segmentation. Using India's INR 100 crore minimum capital requirement as our empirical laboratory, we demonstrate that regulatory constraints generate sharp discontinuities in corporate insurance choices, with implications for insurance market structure and policy design in emerging economies. Our analysis reveals that for corporations with employee populations above 1,000 and predictable claims experience, in-house programs achieve financial viability through elimination of insurer margins and investment income on reserves, provided strong claims governance and appropriate stop-loss coverage are maintained. Base-case break-even around 1,250 employees; 95% CI: 1,050-1,450. However, the current regulatory regime excludes medium-sized enterprises (400-1,000 employees) that would otherwise be viable candidates, creating a policy-relevant market gap. Tiered capital could unlock INR 60,000-67,500 crore in 10-year PV savings. The findings generalize to other emerging markets with similar capital-intensive regulatory frameworks, offering testable thresholds and actionable policy recommendations for regulatory reform.

detail.abstract: This article critically examines Japan's Mobile Software Competition Act (MSCA), enacted in June 2024 and set for enforcement by the Japan Fair Trade Commission (JFTC) in December 2025. Aimed at Apple and Google, the Act imposes ex ante obligations including bans on selfpreferencing, mandatory interoperability, restrictions on app review and payment practices, and controls on pricing and fees, reinforced by detailed JFTC Guidelines issued in July 2025. The article argues that the MSCA departs from market-oriented principles by adopting categorical per se prohibitions rather than the case-by-case, effects-based approach of Japan's Antimonopoly Act. Contrary to the MSCA's premise of entrenched dominance, this article highlights existing rivalry between Apple's integrated ecosystem and Google's open Android model, alongside emerging competition driven by generative AI and device innovation. The analysis shows that rigid regulation risks eroding product differentiation, discouraging innovation, and reducing consumer welfare, while specific provisions-such as Article 6's ban on self-preferencing, Article 7(2)'s mandate to open core OS functions, and Articles 7-8's restrictions on app store, payment, and browser policies-raise additional concerns. These measures undermine intellectual property rights, compromise device security, and deteriorate user convenience, while fee controls distort markets. The MSCA also grants the JFTC broad discretion in highly technical matters, heightening risks of regulatory overreach and micromanagement. The article concludes that Japan's competition concerns are better addressed within the flexible framework of the Antimonopoly Act, as illustrated by recent enforcement against Apple and Google. It recommends that the JFTC pursue a restrained, dialogue-based approach that balances competition, innovation, and consumer safety.

detail.abstract: In June 2025, New Hampshire became one of the few states in the Northeast to repeal its annual vehicle safety inspection requirement, effective January 2026. This new bill brings up several issues and concerns related to roadway safety, city auto inspection revenue and household costs all over the state. This effort looks specifically at those impacts in Nashua and Hillsborough County. Drawing on peer-reviewed literature, stakeholder and citizen testimony, federal reports, and proprietary survey data, the analysis compares data from inspection and non-inspection states and performs statistical tests of fatality rates. 8 out of 10 state combinations found significantly lower fatality rates in inspection states, suggesting some measurable though variable safety benefits. Testimony from local auto shops showed near consensus regarding projected revenue losses and worries about unsafe vehicles on the road, while resident surveys revealed agreement in heavy support of the repeal, due to the cost benefits and perceived ineffectiveness of vehicle inspections. Taking all of these findings into account, we find that while vehicle inspections offer short-term relief, they create long-term safety and small business risks. A better strategy would be changing the program to allow for rotation of inspection between companies, years and technology-oriented inspections.

detail.abstract: This study extends the conceptualization of corporate governance by analyzing its role in crisis management as a response to institutional complexity. Effective governance mechanisms enhance resilience by fostering accountability and strategic adaptability, particularly in volatile environments such as crisis situations. My view is focused on integration of leadership structures and how these structures work towards mitigating uncertainty and facilitates robust decision-making in corporate environments. This research attempts to create a conceptual framework to analyze the intricate role of corporate governance mechanisms-independent directors, dual-class boards, and CEO duality-in shaping organizational resilience and decision-making during times of crises. Independent directors provide monitoring and credibility to report accurate and implementing strong risk management but simultaneously slow down the decision-making process. detail.abstract: Background: This research explores the role of emotional intelligence (EI) in personal and professional success. EI, a multifaceted construct encompassing self-awareness, emotion management, self-motivation, empathy, and social skills, has significantly impacted academic performance, social interactions, and overall well-being. While extensively researched, the influence of cultural and athletic backgrounds on EI still needs to be explored, particularly in non-Western settings. Objectives: This research at P P Savani University at Surat Gujarat focuses on African and Indian students. It aims to assess and contrast emotional intelligence (EI) levels, particularly among athletes and nonathletes. The study investigates the impact of sports participation, cultural aspects, and social support structures and provides suggestions for improving EI and emotional wellness in this specific cultural setting. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 422 students, equally divided among Indian and African athletes and nonathletes. The study assessed EI using validated questionnaires measuring self-awareness, emotion management, self-motivation, empathy, and social skills. Statistical analyses, including t-tests and ANOVA, were performed using SPSS software to analyze the influence of cultural and athletic factors on EI. Results: This study reveals variations in emotional intelligence aspects among the participants. Furthermore, African students scored higher in self-motivation than their counterparts, indicating distinctions in motivational factors. These findings are thoroughly outlined in Table 3 of the results section, which presents the ANOVA analysis supporting these conclusions and showcasing the variance in self-awareness among these groups. Athletes generally demonstrated better social skills than nonathletes. Additionally, African students scored higher in self-motivation than Indian students, highlighting the significant impact of cultural and athletic backgrounds on various EI dimensions. Conclusions: The study's findings have significant practical implications. They underscore the importance of considering cultural and athletic contexts when developing interventions to enhance student EI. detail.abstract: This paper tests whether demographic aging shocks propagate across Japanese municipalities through spatial and economic network channels. Using quarterly panel data on 4,547 municipalities from 2018 to 2024, I apply the spatial treatment effect framework from \citet{kikuchi2024dynamical} and \citet{kikuchi2024stochastic}, extended with a Lévy–Brownian process \footnote{A temporal jump-diffusion process combining continuous Brownian motion with Lévy jumps.} to capture discontinuous crisis events alongside continuous evolution. The central finding contradicts conventional assumptions: aging shocks remain strictly localized with zero spillovers despite connected infrastructure and dense networks. Five analyses establish this result. Perturbative decomposition shows 99.82 percent of variation explained by direct effects. Treatment effect estimates (ATT=0.355pp, ATE=0.541pp) exclude spillover components. General equilibrium multipliers of 1.04 indicate minimal amplification. Stochastic uncertainty quantification reveals that while Lévy jumps raise crisis probability from 3 to 12 percent, tail risk remains localized. Temporal trends document increasing regional isolation. The absence of spillovers reflects fundamental isolation: Tokyo concentration, infrastructure decay, service withdrawal, and economic hollowing transform Japan's spatial structure from integrated to fragmented. Regional coordination policies are ineffective; local interventions are sufficient.

title: Why Suppliers Might Prefer Linear and Secret Vertical Contracts?
affiliations: Tel Aviv University - Buchmann Faculty of Law and Coller School of Management , Tel-Aviv University

detail.title: Why Suppliers Might Prefer Linear and Secret Vertical Contracts?
detail.abstract: We consider suppliers who endogenously choose the type of vertical contract they use with retailers with whom they have interlocking relationships. If contracts are constrained to be linear, suppliers non-cooperatively choose secret contracts instead of public contracts if product substitutability is high. If contracts are constrained to be secret, suppliers may choose linear contracts over two-part tariffs if substitutability is high. When suppliers can choose among four contract types: secret linear, public linear, secret two-part tariffs and public two-part tariffs, choosing public two-part tariffs is a dominant strategy and the unique equilibrium, even though secret linear contracts are more profitable to suppliers when product substitutability is high.

title: Set Shaping Theory: An Extension of Classical Information Theory

detail.title: Set Shaping Theory: An Extension of Classical Information Theory
detail.abstract: The Set Shaping Theory (SST) introduces a combinatorial framework that reformulates the foundations of lossless data compression. While Shannon's classical theory defines coding efficiency in probabilistic terms, SST operates on the structural properties of the sequence space itself. By reshaping the domain of sequences through invertible transformations, SST achieves a reduction in average empirical entropy without requiring prior knowledge of source statistics. This paper outlines the conceptual transition from probabilistic to combinatorial measures of information and discusses how this approach complements, rather than violates, the Shannon framework.

title: Assessing Work-Life Balance among Healthcare Employees: A Study in the Jammu Region, J&K (UT)

detail.title: Assessing Work-Life Balance among Healthcare Employees: A Study in the Jammu Region, J&K (UT)
detail.abstract: Purpose: Work-life balance (WLB) is a crucial component of employee well-being, particularly in high-stress environments such as healthcare. This study explores the factors influencing WLB among healthcare employees in the Jammu region of Jammu and Kashmir (UT). Design/Methodology/Approach: The primary data has been gathered from 150 participants with the help of structured questionnaire. In this analysis, those participants were considered who had given due importance to each question of the study and has given considerable amount of time for each part i.e. 138 valid responses for analysis. The Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) technique, implemented using Smart PLS 3, was considered to estimate the effect to estimate the effect organizational, personal, and social factors on WLB. Findings: Personal factors have a strong and positive influence on work-life balance (WLB), whereas organizational and social factors do not demonstrate a significant effect. This highlights the critical role of individual attributes in shaping WLB among healthcare professionals. Originality: This study offers meaningful insights for policymakers and healthcare administrators by emphasizing the need for targeted strategies that support employee well-being. It underscores the importance of addressing both personal and organizational challenges to foster a more balanced and sustainable work environment.

title: Culture Shock Experiences: A Case Study of a Canadian in Vietnam
affiliations: and Tay Nguyen University

detail.title: Culture Shock Experiences: A Case Study of a Canadian in Vietnam
detail.abstract: Culture shock has always been an important issue. Previous studies on the cultural adaptation process have only focused on the general nature of culture shock. Yet, little attention has been drawn to how expatriates from Englishspeaking countries have undergone culture shock in Vietnam. This paper presents a case study of a native Canadian who had settled in Vietnam for 11 years (up to the time of the study). The study aimed to investigate the aspects of the participant's cultural experience, the factors determining its severity, and the strategies to facilitate the adaptation process. The research involved a case study approach using a semi-structured interview as a main data collection instrument. The findings reveal that (1) five aspects of culture shock were learning the Vietnamese language, joining a close community, detecting smells, using transportation, and observing local behaviors; (2) the factors determining the intensity levels of culture shock included language barriers, communities, personality traits and different regions in Vietnam, while previous overseas experiences had less impact; and (3) to overcome the culture shock, the participant learned the Vietnamese language, made friends with the locals, remained disciplined and kept himself occupied. The findings of this cultural phenomenon could provide helpful insights to English teachers and students interested in language and culture studies.

title: New Brooms Sweep Clean, Old Brooms know the Corners: The Effects of Managerial Replacement on Employee Performance
affiliations: University of Zurich, University of Zurich - Department of Business Administration (IBW), University of Lausanne and University of Zurich - Department of Business Administration (IBW)

detail.title: New Brooms Sweep Clean, Old Brooms know the Corners: The Effects of Managerial Replacement on Employee Performance
detail.abstract: Although managers are frequently replaced, the effects of managerial replacement on individual employee performance remain largely unexplored. By integrating Human Capital Theory (HCT) and Signaling Theory (ST) to examine managerial replacement, we argue that their seemingly opposing implications—HCT is typically associated with a negative effect on performance, while ST is linked with positive outcomes—are, in fact, compatible. We propose that this relationship stems from two distinct facets of employee performance: work quality and work effort. We investigate these effects by analyzing data from the professional soccer industry. Our two-stage least squares instrumental variable regressions confirm the effects derived from our theory integration. First, managerial replacement decreases employee work quality because new managers assign tasks less efficiently. Second, managerial replacement increases employee work effort because employees signal their skills to the new manager. To avoid the negative consequences of managerial replacement without diminishing the positive ones, organizations may consider selecting new managers through internal recruitment, as this approach can efficiently allocate tasks and ideally maintain a sufficient distance from employees to motivate them effectively. We contribute to the succession literature by shifting the focus from the organizational to the individual level, thus offering a plausible explanation for inconsistent findings in prior research.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive conceptual and applied framework for the Strategic Composite Network Theory (SCNT¹)-a paradigm designed to operationalize the management of talent, social capital, and organizational resilience through dynamic, network-based systems. SCNT¹ redefines organizations as adaptive ecosystems composed of interconnected "expert tribes," where trust, knowledge, and creativity circulate organically. By integrating philosophical coherence, network intelligence, and adaptive learning, SCNT¹ offers a new foundation for understanding and guiding postbureaucratic organizations. The present article transforms SCNT¹ into a practical model for strategic design and governance, demonstrating how network intelligence can be cultivated, measured, and aligned with an organization's philosophical core. The paper introduces key analytical tools such as Organizational Network Analysis (ONA), Tribal Collaboration Index (TCI), and Resilience Flow Mapping-each translating theoretical constructs into managerial application. This work also connects SCNT¹ with complementary theories-Philosophical Composite Strategic Theory (PCST²), Seed Growth Strategy Theory (SGST³), and Vectorial Duality of Consciousness (VDC⁴)through an integrated network-interconnected model (Figure 4.4). The findings suggest that when organizations embody philosophical coherence and networked collaboration, they achieve higher adaptability, collective intelligence, and sustainability.

title: The Compliance of the Opt-Out Mediation for Transnational Commercial Disputes with the Right to Human Dignity and the Right to a Fair Trial

detail.title: The Compliance of the Opt-Out Mediation for Transnational Commercial Disputes with the Right to Human Dignity and the Right to a Fair Trial
detail.abstract:
More than a decade after the completion of the transposition period of the European Mediation Directive, the impact of this legislative instrument on transnational commercial disputes remains insignificant. A substantial body of literature suggests that implementing a moderated approach to mandatory mediation could effectively increase the number of mediated transnational commercial disputes. The approach in question relates to the insertion of a nudge into Article 5 of the Mediation Directive.

The paper argues that, although, prima facie, the mitigated mandatory mediation may raise concerns as regards compliance with the right of access to court and human dignity, it is likely to withstand scrutiny from both the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) and the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU), if would be adopted by the European Union in the future. From an empirical standpoint, it is argued that the mitigated mandatory mediation is a type of infringement of human dignity that neither the European Court of Human Rights nor the Court of Justice of the European Union protects. Finally, an analysis of the compatibility of mitigated mandatory mediation with the right to access a court demonstrates that such limitations on fair trial requirements are proportionate.

detail.title: Enhancing Teacher Competence and Performance through Motivation and Organization
detail.abstract: Using teacher competence as a mediating variable, this study examines the effects of self-efficacy, perceived organizational support, and the need for achievement on elementary school teachers' performance. 300 teachers from five different Indonesian provinces participated in a quantitative survey. Data were gathered using a validated and trustworthy Likert scale questionnaire, and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with AMOS was used for analysis. Both directly and indirectly through competence, the results show that all three psychological traits significantly and favorably affect teacher performance. These findings demonstrate how crucial it is to raise teachers' need for achievement, perceived organizational support, self-efficacy cayaasa tin order to raise the standard of elementary education.

detail.abstract: This paper presents "Machineria of Dialogue 2.0," a formalized computational framework for analyzing complex social, technical, and psychological systems. The methodology operationalizes the philosophical concepts of Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari's schizoanalysis, specifically the theories of desiring-machines, the body without organs, and rhizomatics. The core innovation is the introduction of a quantifiable Archaic Layer, modeled as a vector in a 3-dimensional space of Intensity (Vitality, Impulse, Pattern), which captures pre-logical, systemic reflexes and instincts. Complemented by a structured analysis of Dialogic Micro-Machines (DMMs) and their forces, the framework provides a step-by-step algorithm for mapping systems, diagnosing blockages, and identifying points of maximum potential for intervention. This work bridges continental philosophy and practical systems analysis, offering a tool for researchers in sociology, digital humanities, AI ethics, and organizational studies.

title: Place-Based Initiatives and Educational Outcomes: Evidence from India's Aspirational Districts Programme
affiliations: The University of Manchester,  and University of Luxembourg

detail.title: Place-Based Initiatives and Educational Outcomes: Evidence from India's Aspirational Districts Programme
detail.abstract: We evaluate the impact of India's Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP)-a large-scale, multi-sector initiative launched in 2018 to accelerate development in more than 100 of the country's most lagging regions-on educational outcomes. Using a difference-indifferences design and district-representative data from the Annual Status of Education Report (2010-2022), we estimate the programme's effects on schooling participation and learning. We find statistically significant improvements in foundational literacy and numeracy, with larger gains for girls and for children aged eight and above. School participation also increased, with reductions in dropout and neverenrollment among these subgroups. Evidence on mechanisms points to higher teacher and student attendance, consistent with ADP's focus on monitoring, accountability, and cross-sector coordination.

title: How Can Transnational Commercial Mediation, in the Meaning of the Mediation Directive, Be Effectively Promoted?

detail.title: How Can Transnational Commercial Mediation, in the Meaning of the Mediation Directive, Be Effectively Promoted?
detail.abstract:
Mediation provides a great number of gains to its users due some core characteristics of the process such as confidentiality, informality or the fact that the process and its outcome can be tailed to the wish of the parties. Mediation has “advantages in economic terms, by reducing the cost of proceedings, and in social terms, by shortening otherwise lengthy civil proceedings, which can have damaging consequences for the parties”.1 Plus, the non-adversarial nature of the process preserves the relationship of the parties and can subsequently set good precedent for future problem resolution.

In view of the benefits of mediation, it can be argued that the promotion of mediation can contribute to the achievement of policy objectives of the European Union, notably the proper functioning of the internal market2. Indeed, mediation benefits businesses and contributes to the proper functioning of the internal market since the process is rapid, inexpensive and ensures the preservation of commercial relationships.

Despite the adoption of the Mediation Directive, mediation remained an unpopular choice for the resolution of transnational business disputes, in comparison to litigation or arbitration. The paper argues that the Mediation directive failed at encouraging mediation and that a new intervention from the European Union is necessary in order to create rules that effectively raise the number of mediated cross border commercial disputes.

On the basis of empirical and theoretical studies, the research demonstrates that the Directive 2008/52/EC did not lead to positive results because the legislative act was created on the basis of the classical economics approach to lawmaking. Furthermore, it is argued that nudging and framing can be tools for lawmakers in order to effectively increase the utilization of mediation for the resolution of cross border commercial disputes in the meaning of Directive 2008/52/EC.

detail.title: Rating Government Procurement Markets
detail.abstract: We develop a novel, scalable method for assessing the quality of public procurement systems using standard administrative data. Our approach compares the distribution of procurement opportunities to the distribution of contract awards across firms. We first derive a simple theoretical benchmark that relates the expected distribution of contract value winning firms, measured as a Herfindahl-Hirschman index (HHI), to the distribution of auction values, measured as a respective HHI, and the number of winning firms. Significant deviations of winning firms' HHI from this benchmark indicate potential governance failures such as corruption or unchecked collusion. Our method requires no subjective input, is transparent and reproducible, and allows for meaningful comparisons across countries, industry sectors, and over time. We use procurement data from Ukraine and EU member states in 2018-2021 to assess the performance of five large sectors. Results indicate that Ukraine's procurement performance in four of the five sectors is comparable to many other European countries. However, Ukraine's construction sector consistently displays the largest excess concentration among all countries considered, consistent with anecdotal evidence of corruption in this sector. Overall, with minimal data requirements, our method offers a practical tool for cross-sector and cross-country assessment of procurement systems.

title: Determinants of US Inequality: Disparities Within or Between Ethnic Groups?
affiliations: Brown University - Department of Economics and University of Oxford

detail.title: Determinants of US Inequality: Disparities Within or Between Ethnic Groups?
detail.abstract: Is income inequality in the United States primarily driven by disparities between ethnic groups or within them? Contrary to conventional wisdom, this study uncovers a striking and transformative empirical regularity: an overwhelming 96% of contemporary inequality arises from disparities within groups sharing a common ancestral origin, dwarfing the comparatively minor contribution of inequality between groups. This extraordinary pattern persists across time, educational attainment, demographic characteristics, and geographic regions. The findings represent a shift in the empirical understanding of inequality in the United States, revealing that the deepest and most persistent economic divides run within, rather than between, ethnic communities.

title: Dancing in the Dark: Sentiment Shocks and Economic Activity
affiliations: Friedrich Alexander University Erlangen Nuremberg, University of Heidelberg,  and University of Tübingen - Department of Economics

detail.title: Dancing in the Dark: Sentiment Shocks and Economic Activity
detail.abstract: The business cycle is driven by expectations - some justified, some not - as documented by a host of studies. What is less clear are the conditions that make the economy susceptible to "sentiment shocks." In this paper, we document that uncertainty, as measured by forecaster disagreement, is essential. At times when disagreement is low, sentiment shocks hardly matter for economic activity but are fully absorbed by prices. If, instead, disagreement is high, they move activity with little impact on prices. We obtain these results based on time-series data and a theoretical account based on a New Keynesian model with dispersed information.

Digital transformation improves organization performance efficiency, customer experience, and gains competitive advantage in the market. The research investigates the impact of digital transformation on organization performance in retail industry in Cape Town, South Africa. The research investigates key drivers such as operation efficiency, technology advancement, cybersecurity, omnichannel retailing, customer behavior, and data-driven decision-making, enabling the adoption of digital transformation in the retail industry. The research also investigates how digital transformation influence operation efficiency through collaboration, automation, data-driven decision-making, and supply chain management. title: A method for predicting the thermal strength of coke based on feature interaction and nonlinear optimization
affiliations: Taiyuan University of Technology, Taiyuan University of Technology, Taiyuan University of Technology, Taiyuan University of Technology, Taiyuan University of Technology, Taiyuan University of Technology, Taiyuan University of Technology, Taiyuan University of Technology and Taiyuan University of Technology

detail.title: A method for predicting the thermal strength of coke based on feature interaction and nonlinear optimization
detail.abstract: The hot strength of coke in blast furnace operations is critically evaluated by its strength after reaction (Coke Strength after Reaction, CSR) and reactivity (Coke Reactivity Index, CRI). Given that traditional evaluation methods for these properties are often time-consuming, this study focused on developing rapid, accurate predictive models. We aimed to optimize machine learning models for CSR and CRI prediction using an XGBoost-based framework, enhancing interpretability via SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis. We constructed both basic and enhanced XGBoost models; the latter integrated advanced feature engineering, including generating leaf index features from the model's tree structure, and subsequent feature selection. The enhanced models consistently showed superior predictive performance for both CSR and CRI, achieving significantly higher R2 values (e.g., [[EQUATION]],[[EQUATION]]) and lower RMSE and MAE than basic models. SHAP analysis offered crucial insights into feature importance and their contributions, identifying key influencing factors for both properties. Although both properties were predicted accurately, CSR models generally performed slightly better, likely reflecting differences in these properties' inherent complexities. This research demonstrates the robust predictive capabilities of optimized XGBoost models, providing an interpretable, data-driven approach for forecasting essential coke quality parameters, thus facilitating improved control and operational efficiency in industrial coking processes.

title: Wealth Taxation: The Key to Unlocking Capital Gains
affiliations: NHH Norwegian School of Economics - Department of Business and Management Science and NHH Norwegian School of Economics

detail.title: Wealth Taxation: The Key to Unlocking Capital Gains
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes how a wealth tax affects investor portfolio choice when a realization-based capital gains tax is present. We develop a two-period model with heterogeneous investors and show that while a capital gains tax distorts portfolio choice by encouraging investors to postpone realization, a wealth tax can eliminate this distortion and enhance efficient portfolio choice. Our optimal-tax model balances the equity gains from both taxes against efficiency losses related to intertemporal and portfolio choice. We use the model to derive an elasticity-based criterion for empirically evaluating the desirability of a wealth tax.

title: An Empirical Inquiry Into Cartel Overcharges and Cartel Fines Including an Assessment of the EU’s Guidelines on Cartel Fines and Damages

detail.title: An Empirical Inquiry Into Cartel Overcharges and Cartel Fines Including an Assessment of the EU’s Guidelines on Cartel Fines and Damages
detail.abstract: Utilizing Connor’s International Cartel Database and employing difference-in-differences methodology, we find that market concentration, the number of buyers and cartel duration have significant impacts on cartel overcharges. We also find that the European Commission's 2006 guidelines on the method of setting fines for cartel infringements seems to have decreased cartel overcharges in the EU. In addition, the EU’s cartel damages directive of 2014 (2014/104/EU) appear to have increased private damage payments. Overall, we find support that these two changes in EU competition policy have a reversing impact on the otherwise increasing trend of cartel overcharges, as making the infringement more costly at least in the EU.

title: Double orientation integrated cutting tool wear for surface milling multi-directional CFRP with ball-end cutter
affiliations: Dalian University of Technology, Dalian University of Technology, Dalian University of Technology, Dalian University of Technology, Dalian University of Technology and Dalian University of Technology

detail.title: Double orientation integrated cutting tool wear for surface milling multi-directional CFRP with ball-end cutter
detail.abstract: Ball-end milling of carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) curved components is prone to unpredictable and localized excessive tool wear. Conventional strategies for mitigating wear primarily focus on applying tool coatings or optimizing cutting parameters like spindle speeds and feed rates. Through an analysis of the characteristics of both composite materials and ball-end cutters, we have identified that, in addition to the aforementioned methods, modifying the tool path and tool orientation can also enhance tool durability. This approach offers the distinct advantage of improving tool life without compromising machining efficiency or increasing economic costs, and is applicable for further optimization under diverse working conditions. An improved methodology for fitting wear rates was developed, identifying specific fiber cutting angle ranges that exhibit significantly distinct wear characteristics. By employing the relative sliding length as an independent variable, the wear rate at any positional angle can be directly calculated. A predictive wear model was subsequently established by correlating data across different fiber cutting angles, enabling—for the first time—accurate prediction of wear in the milling of curved CFRP surfaces, with a maximum prediction error of less than 14%. Based on this model, the root causes of heterogeneous wear distribution were investigated. The analysis reveals that the frequency of change in the fiber cutting angle and the sequence of engaged fiber orientations directly govern the distribution of tool-workpiece contact conditions. This phenomenon is a unique characteristic of curved-surface milling in composites. This finding and the underlying mechanism provide a novel perspective for enhancing the economic efficiency of machining large-scale CFRP components.

title: Loss Of Tax Residency: And the Importance of Completing the Procedures Before the National Tax Authority in Due Time and Proper Form
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Loss Of Tax Residency: And the Importance of Completing the Procedures Before the National Tax Authority in Due Time and Proper Form
detail.abstract:
The issue of tax residence and its loss constitutes one of the most significant topics in contemporary tax law, not only in Argentina but also in comparative law, as it lies at the intersection of the State’s taxing power, constitutional principles in tax matters, and the international mobility of individuals. Tax residence serves as a fundamental connecting factor because it determines whether a taxpayer is subject to taxation on their worldwide income or, conversely, only on income sourced in Argentina.

In this context, the recent ruling issued in the Gruneisen case by Chamber V of the National Court of Appeals in Federal Administrative Litigation, dated August 21, 2025, provides an opportunity to comprehensively examine the conceptual, normative, and jurisprudential framework governing the matter, as well as to reflect on the practical implications this has for taxpayers’ tax planning.

Addressing this analysis requires consideration of basic principles of tax law which, in their autonomy, were disregarded by the national tax authority in the case under review, thereby leading to an unjust result for the taxpayer—who, compelled to litigate, ultimately received a clear and forceful response from the national courts. Among these principles are the principle of legality, the principle of territoriality, moderate informalism, the distinction between formal and substantive duties, the regulatory powers of the tax administration, and the restrictive interpretation of tax law. All of these will be addressed—albeit briefly—in this paper as a necessary prelude to examining the substantive issue.

Based on the development of these general principles that inform tax law, we then turn to the core issue (loss of tax residence and its conditions) to highlight the importance of proper tax registration and accurate declaration of the taxpayer’s fiscal situation before the national tax authority.

title: VCLT and the Peaceful Coexistence of Tax and Investment Treaties: a Case Study of Limited MFN Clauses and the FET Standard

detail.title: VCLT and the Peaceful Coexistence of Tax and Investment Treaties: a Case Study of Limited MFN Clauses and the FET Standard

keywords: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties

publicationDetails.detailsText: World Tax Journal, volume 17, issue 1, 2024[10.59403/32xh33c]

detail.abstract:
The general purpose of this article is to demonstrate that customary international law (CIL) has a significant role to play in connecting international tax law and international investment law. Bridging a gap between those sources of international law is not only an important endeavour in the theory of law but also in practice. This article purports to achieve the abovementioned general purpose by focusing on the application of the rule and principles of interpretation under the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (VCLT), which represent a codification of CIL, to limited most favoured nation (MFN) clauses in tax treaties. The hypothesis of the authors is that a serious failure in a proper application of the VCLT to interpret the MFN clauses in tax treaties may lead to a violation of international investment agreements (IIAs), in particular the fair and equitable treatment (FET) standard. The analysis and conclusions are relevant to all tax treaties and IIAs containing the MFN clause and FET standard, respectively. They are also of relevance for the interpretation of all provisions of tax treaties, not only the limited MFN clauses, in accordance with the VCLT. Examining tax treaties through the lens of the FET standard allows the FET standard to be seen as a gateway for the systemic integration of tax treaties in accordance with the principle enshrined in article 31(3) (c) of the VCLT, because some of core elements of that standard are deeply rooted in sources of international law (general principles of law and custom).

title: Infrastructure Development as a Factor in Increasing the Competitiveness of the Region

detail.title: Infrastructure Development as a Factor in Increasing the Competitiveness of the Region
detail.abstract:
The aim of the research is to define the place of infrastructure in the development of a particular region. Structural production and non-production elements are the subjects of the integrated system of the national economy of the state, which reflects the level of development of the population in a particular region and the whole country, and also creates conditions for the realization of human potential. Public infrastructure, being a structural link of the economy, is responsible for the production and distribution of public goods aimed at the formation and development of the potential of the national economy. 

In order to assess the impact of infrastructure on the competitiveness of the region, three main approaches were analyzed: by M. Porter ("Competitive Rhombus"), the International Institute for Management Development and the World Economic Forum. M. Porter believes that infrastructure is the most important element of the "diamond", in particular, the group of "factor conditions". In the competitiveness ranking, infrastructure accounts for the largest share of factors (106 out of 334, or 32%). In the WEF Global Competitiveness Ranking, infrastructure is singled out as a separate group of factors (12 factors, second only to the Institutions group in terms of their number). A comparative analysis of these three approaches showed that despite the difference in approaches to the content of the concept of "infrastructure", everyone recognizes the special importance of infrastructure development for the growth of competitiveness, and among other factors, it is infrastructure that has the highest "weight" in assessing competitiveness. 

Thus, a developed and sustainable infrastructure complex is one of the key factors in the socio-economic development of the region, forming relationships between economic entities and members of society in relation to the consumption of goods and services necessary for the development of human capital, improving the quality and standard of living, and economic growth of the region.
